articles.title: Zazu sleep trainers Sam and Davy: common questions
articles.text:
Help with the buttons, eyes, wake-up settings and batteries on Sam the Lamb and Davy the Dog, plus the manuals and quick-start videos.
Buttons and key lock
The buttons do not react when I press them. What is wrong?
The key lock is probably on. To unlock, press the key lock button on the right for 3 seconds.
The key lock turns on automatically when the buttons have not been touched for 30 seconds. This stops the settings being changed by accident.
How can I stop my child playing with the buttons and changing the settings?
The clock enters key lock mode automatically after 30 seconds. To turn it on yourself, press the key lock button for 3 seconds.
When you start the sleep timer or wake-up time, the key lock turns on straight away so the settings cannot be changed.
Eyes and wake-up time
How can I close Sam's or Davy's eyes?
In the menu, choose the time Sam or Davy will close their eyes each day. To close them earlier, press the DOWN button for 3 seconds.
How do I open Sam's or Davy's eyes manually?
Unlock the device first, then hold the UP button for 3 seconds.
Can I switch off the orange screen that comes on half an hour before wake-up?
No. It cannot be switched off and the timing is fixed at 30 minutes.
If your child is still asleep, the orange light will not wake them. If they do wake, the orange screen tells them it is not much longer until wake-up time.
Can I separate the wake-up time from the alarm time?
Yes. When you set the nap time or wake-up time, you can set the alarm separately. This lets the sound alarm go off later than the eyes open.
Power and batteries
My sleep trainer does not work on batteries.
Use new alkaline batteries from a known brand, and change to a fresh set to be sure they are full. Some batteries, such as zinc-carbon batteries, do not have enough power to move the eyes.
My sleep trainer keeps resetting by itself.
The batteries are the most likely cause. Make sure they are not nearly empty, and do not use zinc-carbon batteries. Use new alkaline batteries from a good brand.
If the power goes off, does the sleep trainer remember its settings?
Only if batteries are fitted. We suggest keeping batteries in the sleep trainer as a backup in case the power goes off.

articles.title: Zazu wall lights Fay, Rex and Otis: common questions
articles.text:
How to switch your Zazu wall light on and off, change the brightness, charge it and fix the most common problems.
Using the light
How do I switch it on or off?
Swipe your hand underneath the light and it will switch on or off.
Hand gestures only work when the ON/OFF switch on the light is set to ON. If it is set to OFF, the light will not turn on.
How do I change the brightness?
Hold your hand still within 20 cm below the motion sensor. While your hand is there, the light slowly dims and brightens. Take your hand away when it reaches the brightness you want.
How do I charge the light?
The light runs on a built-in rechargeable battery that is charged with the USB cable supplied. When the battery is nearly empty, the small charging light flickers red. It stays lit while charging and switches off when the battery is full.
Use only the USB cable that came with the light, and keep the cable out of reach of children, as long cables are a strangulation hazard.
Fixing problems
The light dims or switches off by itself.
Make sure nothing is within 60 cm below the motion sensor, as it can interfere with the sensor.
The light switches off after a while.
Check the timer switch. When it is set to 20 or 45, the light switches off by itself after 20 or 45 minutes. Set it to OFF and the light stays on until you switch it off.
The small animals do not stay on the light.
Each animal clicks onto the light with a magnet. If one no longer stays in place, send us a request and our team will help.
The animals contain magnets. Keep them away from small children, as swallowed or inhaled magnets can cause serious injury. Seek medical help straight away if this happens.

articles.title: Zazu bedtime projectors: common questions
articles.text:
How the 3-step sleep program and cry sensor work on the Zazu ocean projectors Cody and Otto, how to wash the plush cover, and the manuals for each projector.
The sleep program
How does the 3-step sleep program work?
Phase one: waves and orange fish swim around the room while soothing ocean sounds play. This catches your baby's attention.
Phase two: the light is dimmer, the waves keep moving and only a few fish swim around the room. The sound changes to underwater bubbles.
Phase three: the waves are calm, the fish are sleeping and there is no sound, ready for sleep.
The whole program takes 30 minutes and then switches off by itself.
Sometimes there are fewer fish. Is that right?
Yes. From phase two of the sleep program only a few fish swim around the room, to make a quieter setting for falling asleep.
How long does the cry sensor work?
Each time you start a new sleep program, the cry sensor is active for 12 hours. You need to switch the cry sensor on first, using the switch on the bottom of the module.
When the cry sensor hears crying, the sleep program restarts from phase two to settle your baby again.
Can I use Cody or Otto without sound?
Yes. On the bottom of the module there is a music choice switch. Set it to OFF.
Care
Can the plush cover be washed?
Yes. Remove the module first, then hand wash the plush cover and let it air dry.

articles.title: Zazu Robby the Rocker pram rocker: charging, fitting and use
articles.text:
Robby the Rocker straps onto your pram or stroller handlebar and gently rocks it so your baby can keep napping. Here is how to charge it, fit it properly and get the best rocking.
Charging Robby
Charge Robby fully before you use it for the first time.
Take Robby off the pram before you charge it.
Open the charging lid and plug in the supplied cable, connected to a standard 5V USB adapter of no more than 2A or 10W. Robby does not support fast chargers.
The indicator light is red while Robby charges and switches off when the battery is full, after about 2 to 2.5 hours.
Unplug the cable and close the charging lid so water cannot get in.
Robby does not run while it is charging. When the battery light starts blinking, there are about two hours of use left, depending on the speed you have chosen. A full charge gives about 15 rocking cycles at the highest speed, so the lowest speed that works will make the battery last longer. The rechargeable battery cannot be replaced.
Fitting Robby to the pram
Park the pram on a flat, level surface and lock the brakes.
Hold Robby under the main horizontal handlebar, with the buckle facing your child (the cry sensor is on that side) and the buttons facing you.
Push the strap into the buckle until it clicks, then feed it through as far as it will go by hand.
Lift the large black lever to tighten the strap one notch at a time until Robby is held firmly.
Robby must hang level on the main handlebar, never on a side bar or at an angle, as this weakens the rocking and shortens the life of the motor. Extending the handlebar as far as it goes gives the best rocking. To remove Robby, switch the cry sensor off, hold Robby underneath with one hand and press the small black lever until the strap releases. Make sure your baby is not underneath in case it slips.
Rocking speeds and the cry sensor
Press the plus button to start rocking. The red light above it shows Robby is running.
Use the plus and minus buttons to choose from five speeds. Robby remembers the last speed you used.
Rocking stops by itself after 40 minutes. To stop sooner, hold the minus button until the light goes off.
Press the red ZAZU button to turn on the cry sensor. It stays on for 3 hours and rocks the pram for 10 minutes each time it hears crying.
In noisy places the cry sensor can react to sounds other than crying.
If the rocking feels weak, check that Robby is charged and level, extend the handlebar and take heavy bags or shopping off the pram.
The motor can get a little louder over time. This is normal for this type of motor.
Safety first
Robby can be used from birth to 3 years on prams and strollers. It is not a replacement for a caregiver, so never leave your child unattended. Always use the lowest speed that suits your pram and child, never fit Robby directly above your child or within reach, and do not open it. Robby handles light rain only, so take it off and keep it dry if rain sets in. It suits temperatures from minus 10 to 30 degrees Celsius, and cold weather shortens the battery life.

articles.title: Zazu Sarah the Rabbit sleep trainer: set-up and settings
articles.text:
Sarah the Rabbit helps children learn when to stay in bed and when it is okay to get up: her eyes close at bedtime and open at wake-up time. Set her up once and she runs on her own every day.
Set the clock
Unlock the buttons: hold the key lock (music) button until the padlock disappears from the screen.
Hold the TIME button for 3 seconds.
Choose 12 or 24 hour time with the arrows and confirm with TIME.
Set the hours, minutes, year, month and day in turn, confirming each one with TIME.
Set bedtime and wake-up time
With the buttons unlocked, hold the ALARM button for 3 seconds.
Set the sleep time. This is when the eyes close, and the red nightlight and a sleep sound can play for 30 minutes.
Choose the sleep melody and its volume. Choose 0 for no sound at bedtime.
Set the wake-up time. This is when the eyes open and the light can turn green.
Choose the wake-up alarm sound and its volume. Choose 0 for no alarm.
Set the brightness of the orange light that shows before wake-up time and of the green light at wake-up time. Choose 0 to turn either light off.
Press the ALARM button to choose what is active: sleep time only, sleep time and wake-up time, wake-up time only, or nothing. The screen shows which is on.
Set or change the wake-up time before bedtime. Changing it after bedtime can leave Sarah in the wake state until the next cycle.
Nightlight, sounds and snooze
Tap the silicone shell to turn on the nightlight. Keep tapping to step through white, red, pink, blue, multicolour and off.
The nightlight you turn on by hand switches off after 30 minutes, or tap until it is off.
With the buttons unlocked and no music playing, the right arrow changes the nightlight brightness and the left arrow changes the screen brightness.
If you turn the screen fully off, it lights up again at wake-up time.
Press the music button to play a sound for 30 minutes. Press the arrows to change song and hold them to change the volume.
When the alarm sounds, tap the shell to snooze for 5 minutes. The alarm stops by itself after 1 minute.
Charging and care
Sarah comes with a USB cable. Connect it to a good quality adapter: a red light shows while Sarah charges and goes off when charging is complete. Sarah is for indoor use and is not water resistant, so wipe her with a damp cloth and never put her in water.
Good to know
Sarah suits children from about 2 years, when they can follow a simple rule like waiting for the green light. She is not a toy and should be used with adult supervision. Keep the USB cable out of reach, as long cables are a strangulation hazard.

articles.title: Zazu white noise soft toys Dex, Liz, Don and Robin: common questions
articles.text:
Dex the Dog, Liz the Lamb, Don the Donkey and Robin the Racoon, a comforter blanket, each hold a small sound module that plays a heartbeat, white noise, nature sounds or lullabies to help your baby settle.
Getting started
Take the sound module out of the plush. On Dex, Liz and Don it sits in the belly.
Fit 3 AAA alkaline batteries (not included). Do not use zinc carbon batteries.
Turn the module on with the on and off button.
Choose a sound: a loop of three lullabies, nature sounds, a heartbeat or white noise.
Set the volume with the volume button.
Put the module back in the plush.
The sound switches off by itself after 10 minutes.
Cry sensor and shake sensor
Press the cry sensor button to turn it on. It stays active for 12 hours.
When the cry sensor hears crying, it plays the last sound again.
Distance and objects between the toy and your baby reduce the cry sensor's sensitivity.
Turn on the shake sensor if you would like to restart the last sound by gently shaking the toy.
Switch the module off completely when you are not using it.
Robin the Racoon extras
Robin is a comforter blanket as well as a white noise toy. A velcro strap holds your baby's dummy, and a velcro loop lets you hang Robin up. Robin uses the same buttons, sounds, timer and sensors as Dex, Liz and Don.
Washing and care
Always take the sound module out before washing the plush.
Hand wash the plush and let it air dry.
Wipe the module with a damp cloth only. It is not water resistant and must not go in water.
Take out flat batteries, and do not mix old and new batteries or different battery types.
Safety
Do not place the toy inside the cot or too close to your baby. Batteries should only be fitted by an adult, and children should never play with them.

articles.title: Zazu Suzy portable baby soother: sounds, timer and fitting
articles.text:
Suzy is a small portable soother that plays sounds familiar from the womb, so your baby can settle in the pram, the car seat or the cot at home.
Getting started
Fit 3 AAA alkaline batteries (not included). Do not use zinc carbon batteries.
Press the power button to switch Suzy on.
Choose a sound: shushing, white noise, heartbeat, ocean, lullabies or lounge music.
Press the volume button several times to step to the level you want.
Timer and cry sensor
The sound switches off by itself after 20 minutes.
Press the cry sensor button to turn it on. A red light shows it is on, then goes out after 1 minute to save energy, but the sensor stays active for 12 hours.
When Suzy hears crying, she plays the last sound again.
The further Suzy is from your child, the less sensitive the cry sensor is.
Switch Suzy off when you are not using her.
Attaching Suzy
Use the red velcro strap that comes with Suzy. Thread it through the loop on the back and fasten it around the pram, cot or car seat frame.
Keep the volume low, about the level of a soft shower. If you have to raise your voice to talk over it, turn it down.
Care and batteries
Suzy is not water resistant, so keep her dry.
Clean Suzy with a damp cloth and never put her in water.
Take out flat batteries, and do not mix old and new batteries or different battery types.
Do not take Suzy apart if she stops working.
Battery safety
Batteries should only be fitted by an adult. Keep Suzy's batteries out of reach of small children and never let a child play with them.

articles.title: Zazu Emmy the Elephant breathing light: settings and power
articles.text:
Emmy the Elephant combines a breathing light and sound, a red nightlight and a sound machine. Your child watches the light on the ceiling grow and shrink and follows its slow breathing rhythm while falling asleep.
Power and switching on
Emmy runs from the included USB cable connected to a compatible adapter (5V, maximum 3A), or from 3 AA alkaline batteries (not included).
When the USB cable is connected, the batteries are not used.
On batteries, use good quality alkaline batteries, the lowest nightlight brightness and the 20 minute timer for longer battery life.
Press the round button on the front, between Emmy's paws, to switch her on or off. She starts with the settings you used last.
Breathing light and nightlight
Breathing button: choose pulse light and breathing sound, pulse light only, breathing sound only, or off.
Frequency switch: 19 breaths per minute is generally suitable up to about 2 to 6 years, and 22 breaths per minute up to about 1 to 2 years.
Elephant button: sets the red nightlight to low, medium, high or off.
The breathing sound cannot be played at the same time as the sound machine melodies.
Sounds, timer and cry sensor
Music button: choose lullabies, white noise, African lounge or off.
Volume button: low, medium or high.
Timer switch: the light and music switch off after 20 or 40 minutes. Set the switch to off to keep them on all night.
Cry sensor switch: set it to on and the sensor is active for 12 hours. It starts after a 30 second delay, so it does not react while you put Emmy down.
Pressing the front button restarts the 12 hour cry sensor period.
Switching Emmy off with the front button does not turn off the cry sensor. Slide the cry sensor switch to off to stop it.
Good to know
Emmy is not a toy. The light is bright, so do not stare into it. Keep the cable out of reach, as long cables are a strangulation hazard. Emmy is not water resistant: wipe her with a damp cloth and never put her in water.

articles.title: Zazu sunset projectors Tim, Henry and Shally: common questions
articles.text:
Tim the Turtle, Henry the Hedgehog and Shally the Sparrow project a sunset with birds flying around the room, then gently wind down over 30 minutes so your child can drift off.
Setting up
Take the module out of the plush and fit 3 AA alkaline batteries (not included). Do not use zinc carbon batteries.
Put the module back in the plush.
Open the velcro on the bottom to reach the button and sliders.
Place the projector 1 to 2.5 metres from the walls and ceiling for the best projection.
Press the big button to start the sleep program.
The 3-step sleep program
Step 1, 0 to 10 minutes: Bright sunset, birds flying around the room and soothing African sunset music
Step 2, 10 to 20 minutes: Lower brightness, fewer birds and calmer music
Step 3, 20 to 30 minutes: No movement and no sound
Auto-off: The whole program switches off after 30 minutes
If the sky stops moving, that is the program stepping down, not a fault.
Sound and cry sensor
Slider B chooses the sound: off (no music), African sunset music, lullabies or heartbeat.
Slider C sets the volume to high or low.
Slider D turns the cry sensor on or off. When it hears crying, the program restarts from step 2 to settle your child again.
The cry sensor stays active for 12 hours.
Care and batteries
Take the module out, then hand wash the plush and let it air dry.
Wipe the module with a damp cloth only. It is not water resistant.
When the batteries run low, the projection gets weaker and some features may stop working. Replace all three with new alkaline batteries.
Switch the projector off completely when it is not in use.
Safety
Do not place the projector inside the cot or too close to your baby. Batteries should only be fitted by an adult, and children should never play with them.

articles.title: Zazu star projectors Ruby, Leo and Polly: common questions
articles.text:
Ruby the Rabbit, Leo the Lion and Polly the Polar Bear project a starry sky onto the ceiling with soothing melodies, then switch themselves off.
Setting up
Take the module out of the plush and fit 3 AA alkaline batteries (not included). Do not use zinc carbon batteries.
Set the on and off switch on the module to on.
Put the module back in the plush.
Stars, melodies and volume
Press the projection button to start the stars. Press it again to change colour.
The projection switches off after 30 minutes.
Press the music button to play a melody, and press again to change melody. The music switches off after 15 minutes.
Press the volume button once or twice to switch between loud and soft.
For stars without sound, press only the projection button.
Cry sensor
Hold the cry sensor button for 3 seconds to switch it on or off.
A green light flickers for a few seconds when the cry sensor turns on.
When it hears crying, the last melody plays again.
The cry sensor stays active for 12 hours each time you start the projector.
Distance and objects between the projector and your baby reduce its sensitivity.
Care and tips
Take the module out, then hand wash the plush and let it air dry.
Wipe the module with a damp cloth only. It is not water resistant.
Switch the module off completely when it is not in use.
Let the timer end the projection rather than restarting it. A projector also needs a darkish ceiling, so a blackout curtain helps on light summer evenings.
Safety
Do not place the projector inside the cot or too close to your baby. Batteries should only be fitted by an adult, and children should never play with them.

articles.title: WonderFold W4 Luxe stroller wagon: common questions
articles.text:
Sizes, weights, seating and cleaning for the WonderFold W4 Luxe stroller wagon.
About the W4 Luxe
What is the difference between the W4 Luxe and the W4 Elite?
The Luxe and Elite share the same frame and seats.
The Luxe comes with XL all-terrain wheels. The XL all-terrain wheels are also sold separately and fit all W4 models, including the Elite.
The Luxe comes with magnetic 5-point harnesses.
Does the W4 Luxe fit through standard doorways?
Yes. The W4 is 74 cm at its widest point and fits through a standard doorway.
What material is the wagon made from?
100% polyester.
Seats
Does the W4 have raised seats?
Yes, the W4 has raised seats.
Is there a single seat option?
Yes. A single seat is sold as an accessory for the W4 Elite and W4 Luxe.
Every WonderFold stroller wagon sold in Australia is certified to AS 2088:2022 / A1:2024.
What age can my child ride in the wagon?
From 6 months. With a compatible capsule on the car seat adapter, it can be used from birth.
Weights and limits
What is the weight capacity?
The maximum total weight capacity is 136 kg.
What is the weight limit for each bench?
44.9 kg per bench. Each bench has 2 seats, and no more than 4 children should ride at a time.
Is there a height limit?
The wagon is not intended for children taller than 101.6 cm.
How much can I carry in the basket and pockets?
No more than 5 kg in the rear basket and 0.5 kg in each pocket.
Safety
Use the harness at all times and adjust the shoulder straps to fit your child.
Carry no more than 4 children, and spread the weight evenly.
Use the wrist tether strap, and put the brakes on whenever the wagon is stationary.
Never leave the wagon unattended on a slope, even with the brake on.
Use it on flat or gently sloping ground at no more than a brisk walking pace. Never take it on stairs or escalators, and never run, jog or skate with it.
Do not let children climb in unassisted, play on the wagon or hang onto it.
Keep children and fingers clear when folding and unfolding.
Use only WonderFold approved accessories, as hanging bags or other items can make the wagon unstable.
Never leave a harness buckled when no child is in it.
Cleaning
How do I clean my wagon?
Frame: clean with a soft towel, lukewarm water and a mild cleaning solution, then wipe off any remaining water with a dry cloth.
Wheels: clean the wheels regularly with water and remove any dirt, then wipe off any remaining water with a dry cloth.
Fabric: spot clean with mild soap and warm water, then air dry.

articles.title: WonderFold W2 Luxe Pro stroller wagon: common questions
articles.text:
The W2 Luxe Pro is the lightest two-seat WonderFold, with an aluminium frame, all-terrain XL wheels and seats that can face forward or face you. Here are the answers W2 Luxe Pro owners ask for most.
Sizes and limits
Seats: 2
Age: From 6 months in the seats
Child height: Up to 120 cm
Wagon weight: 22.3 kg with seats
Carries: 91 kg in total
Widest point: 76.2 cm
Rear cooler basket: 5 kg in the cooler, 1 kg in the mesh
Storage pockets: 0.5 kg in each pocket
Frame: Lightweight aluminium
Safety standard: AS 2088:2022 / A1:2024
At 76.2 cm across its widest point, the W2 Luxe Pro fits through a standard Australian internal door. For a baby under 6 months, the W2 Car Seat Adapter takes a compatible infant capsule. The adapter is made for the W2 Elite and Luxe, so send us a request before you buy and our team will confirm the fit on your Luxe Pro.
What the Luxe Pro finish adds
A lighter aluminium frame than the Elite and Luxe finishes.
Raised, reclining seats that can face forward or face you, each with a padded 5-point harness.
Front wheels that swivel or lock straight, and all-terrain XL wheels with suspension.
An adjustable faux leather handlebar for parents of different heights.
An insulated rear cooler basket, plus storage pockets on every side.
A deep carriage with mesh sides, a roll-out wind and privacy shade and a front zip door so children can climb in.
A removable UPF 50+ canopy on adjustable poles.
In the box, set-up and folding
Stroller wagon.
Seats with safety harness pads.
All-terrain XL wheels.
UPF 50+ canopy set.
Rear cooler basket.
Baseboard.
Pull strap with handle.
Assembly takes minutes. The W2 Luxe Pro user manual and an assembly video are linked under User guides on the product page. The pull strap clips to the front bottom crossbar and gives you extra help on rough paths. To fold the wagon:
Take out the seats and the canopy, then flip the side pockets into the wagon.
Stand in front of the wagon and press the buttons on either side of the frame.
Hold the folding hinges on both sides and lift them up until the wagon is completely folded.
Secure the lower latch to lock the wagon folded. It then stands on its own for storage.
Cleaning and care
Frame: clean with a soft towel, lukewarm water and a mild cleaning solution, then wipe off any remaining water with a dry cloth.
Wheels: rinse dirt off the wheels regularly with water, then wipe them dry.
Fabric (100% polyester): spot clean with a mild soap and warm water solution, then let it air dry.
Safety first
Buckle every child into their 5-point harness, keep to 91 kg in total and never carry more than 2 children. Slide your hand through the wrist tether strap whenever you push the wagon, and apply the brake whenever you stop. Never leave the wagon unattended on a slope, even with the brake on.

articles.title: WonderFold W4 Luxe Pro stroller wagon: common questions
articles.text:
The W4 Luxe Pro carries up to four children on two benches, on a lighter aluminium frame with XL wheels and seats that can face forward or face each other. Here are the answers W4 Luxe Pro owners ask for most.
Sizes and limits
Seats: 4, on two benches
Age: From 6 months in the seats
Child height: Up to 120 cm

Carries: 136 kg in total
Widest point: 74 cm
Inside the carriage: 84 x 53 cm
Folded: 113 x 74 x 51 cm

At 74 cm wide it rolls through a standard Australian internal door. Before a road trip, measure your boot opening and floor with the parcel shelf out and compare them with the folded size, or use the boot check on the Find your size page. For a baby under 6 months, the W4 Car Seat Adapter takes a compatible infant capsule. The adapter is made for the W4 Elite and Luxe, so send us a request before you buy and our team will confirm the fit on your Luxe Pro.
Four ways to set up the seats
Face to face: the benches face each other so the children can see and chat to each other.
All facing forward: on the Luxe Pro, both benches can face the direction of travel, bus-style.
One bench out: lift a bench out for legroom, a capsule adapter or a floor to rest on.
Open carriage: take the seats out and use the deep carriage for beach gear and big shops.
Every seat reclines and has a padded 5-point harness. The adjustable faux leather handlebar suits parents of different heights, and the front wheels swivel or lock straight.
In the box and folding
Stroller wagon.
Bench seats with safety harness pads.
All-terrain XL wheels.
UPF 50+ canopy set.
Rear cooler basket.
Baseboard.
Pull strap with handle.
Assembly takes minutes, and the W4 Luxe Pro user manual and assembly video are linked under User guides on the product page. To fold the wagon:
Take out the seats and the canopy, then flip the side pockets into the wagon.
Stand in front of the wagon and press the buttons on either side of the frame.
Hold the folding hinges on both sides and lift them up until the wagon is completely folded.
Secure the lower latch to lock the wagon folded. It then stands on its own for storage.
Cleaning and care
Frame: clean with a soft towel, lukewarm water and a mild cleaning solution, then wipe off any remaining water with a dry cloth.
Wheels: rinse dirt off the wheels regularly with water, then wipe them dry.
Fabric (100% polyester): spot clean with a mild soap and warm water solution, then let it air dry.
Safety first
Keep to 136 kg in total and never carry more than 4 children. Buckle every child into their harness, slide your hand through the wrist tether strap whenever you push the wagon, and apply the brake when you stop. Never leave the wagon unattended on a slope, even with the brake on.

articles.title: WonderFold car seat adapter: using an infant capsule on the W2 or W4
articles.text:
The WonderFold seats are suitable from 6 months, so younger babies travel in a compatible infant capsule on the W2 or W4 car seat adapter. This guide covers which capsules fit and how the adapter works.
Which capsules fit
The adapter was designed and safety tested to fit these infant capsules only:
Maxi-Cosi Mico 6.
Maxi-Cosi Mico 12.
Maxi-Cosi AP/Plus models.
Joie i-Gemm.
Nuna Pipa.
Cybex Cloud Q.
Check your capsule model against this list before you buy an adapter.
Which wagon it fits
The W2 Car Seat Adapter fits the W2 Elite and W2 Luxe.
The W4 Car Seat Adapter fits the W4 Elite and W4 Luxe.
If you have a W2 Luxe Pro or W4 Luxe Pro, send us a request before you buy so our team can confirm the fit.
No car seat adapter is sold for the W6.
How the adapter works
It attaches to one side of the wagon, leaving the other side free for a seat or bench.
Lift out the seat or bench on that side to make room for it.
A safety strap adds safety and stability. Always fasten it.
It rotates through 360 degrees in 90 degree steps, so the capsule can face four different directions.
On the W4 only, you can remove both benches and fit two adapters for two capsules.
It folds with the stroller wagon.
Follow the fitting instructions that come with your adapter and your capsule.
Age and safety
The wagon seats are suitable from 6 months. Younger babies should travel only in a compatible capsule on the adapter. Use only the capsules listed above and always fasten the adapter's safety strap.

articles.title: WonderFold canopies and weather covers: rain, wind, cold, sun and bugs
articles.text:
Every WonderFold comes with a removable UPF 50+ canopy and a roll-out wind and privacy shade. For rain, cold, strong sun or insects there is a range of extra covers and nets made to fit the W2 and W4.
The canopy and the Flex Canopy
The standard canopy is UPF 50+, removable and sits on adjustable poles so you can shade the children from any angle. The carriage also has mesh sides and a roll-out wind and privacy shade.
The Flex Canopy, made in a W2 and a W4 size, gives fuller coverage:
Water-resistant fabric with enhanced ventilation.
A removable front and back.
Adjustable side panels that open to reveal mesh sides.
Storage pockets for small essentials.
Easy to install.
Covers for rain, wind and cold
Rain Cover (W2 and W4): a transparent, light and portable sheet with small ventilation holes on the sides and a Velcro entrance for loading and unloading.
Wind Cover (W2 and W4): thinner than the Winter Cover, made for a slightly chilly day.
Winter Cover (W2 and W4): keeps the children warm and cosy and shuts out the cold.
Weather Cover (W4 only): one cover for rain, wind, cold and dust, in a breathable fabric with mesh windows.
Sun and insects
Shadenet (W2 and W4): a lightweight four-sided net that adds partial 360 degree shade on very sunny days. The mesh sides keep air moving and let the children see out, and it is easy to store.
Mosquito Net (W2 and W4): protects the children from insects and is easy to install.
Each cover and net is made for a specific wagon size, so choose the W2 or W4 version to match your wagon. If you have a Luxe Pro or a W6, send us a request before you buy and our team will confirm which covers fit.
Watch the temperature
Airflow under the Weather Cover can be limited even though the fabric breathes. Always check your child's comfort and open the mesh windows in hot or humid conditions. Keep a close eye on your child under any cover.

articles.title: WonderFold warranty, registration and spare parts
articles.text:
Every new WonderFold stroller wagon sold in Australia is looked after by our team at Coolkidz Australia in Braeside. Here is how the warranty works, how to register your wagon and what to do if something is not right.
What the warranty covers
Every new WonderFold stroller wagon comes with a one-year manufacturer warranty against manufacturing defects. It covers defects in materials or workmanship for one year from the date of purchase, for the original owner using the wagon as the manual directs. It does not cover damage from alterations, misuse or abuse. This is on top of your rights under Australian Consumer Law, which always apply.
Registering your wagon
Find the serial number on the sticker on the frame.
Have your purchase date, the store you bought from and your receipt ready. A phone photo or a PDF of up to 4 MB is fine.
Open the Warranty Registration page and enter your details, the model, the colour, the serial number and the purchase date.
Upload your receipt and submit the form. You will receive a copy by email.
Your receipt is kept on file, so you will not need to find it again if you ever make a claim.
Your model, serial number and purchase date are ready when you contact us, which makes claims faster.
You receive safety updates directly from us, not through a retailer.
Making a claim or ordering parts
Send us a request with your order number and the model of your wagon.
Add photos or a short video that show the issue.
If your wagon arrived faulty or you received the wrong item, send your request within 48 hours of delivery. We will send a return authority within 1 to 2 working days, then replace, repair or refund and reimburse the return postage.
In warranty, we repair or replace. Out of warranty, we can quote spare parts such as wheels, brakes, canopy poles and fabric, and seats.
Before you send anything back
Please do not post a wagon or part back to us without a return authority. Send us a request first and we will tell you exactly what to do.

articles.title: Gaia Baby Hera Cot Bed: common questions
articles.text:
Colours, ages, mattress heights and dimensions for the Gaia Baby Hera Cot Bed.
About the cot
What colours does the cot come in?

Once your baby can push up on their hands or starts to pull up using the side of the cot, you must move the base to the lower position, and always before your baby can sit up unaided. The lower position is the safest position for the cot base.
The cot bed suits about birth to 3 years, the toddler bed about 3 to 4 years and the first bed about 4 to 5 years. Once your child can climb out of the cot, stop using it as a cot and convert it straight away to the toddler bed or first bed.
Size and what is in the box

Width: 64 cm
Height: 93.4 cm
Weight: 29 kg
What is in the box?
Everything you need to build the cot, including the parts to convert it to a toddler bed and first bed.

Yes. The Hera Cot comes with an Australian-made, GECA-certified mattress.

articles.title: Gaia Baby Serena Convertible Cot Bed: stages and set-up
articles.text:
The Serena Convertible Cot Bed is part of Gaia Baby's patented 8-in-1 growth system. One solid birch frame takes your child from a newborn cot to a first bed, and the Australian-made mattress is included.
The four stages
All the parts for these stages come in the box:
Cot bed with the mattress in the high position: birth to about 6 months.
Cot bed with the mattress in the low position: about 6 months to 3 years.
Toddler bed: about 3 to 4 years.
First bed: about 4 to 5 years.
The Junior Bed Extension, sold separately, extends the frame into a junior bed and takes the system to 7+ years. The Serena Toddler Rail, also sold separately, adds extra security once your child is in the toddler or first bed.
Lowering the mattress
Use the top base position for your newborn. Once your baby can push up on their hands, roll over or pull up on the sides, usually at around 6 months, you must move the base to the bottom position, and always before your baby can sit up unaided. The bottom position is the safest position for the cot base.
When your child is able to climb out, stop using it as a cot and convert it straight away to the toddler bed or first bed. In the toddler bed one side panel comes off so your child can climb in and out, and the other side panel must always stay in place.
Assembly and care
The cot bed arrives in three boxes.
An Allen key is supplied. You will also need a cross head screwdriver.
Do not fully tighten the bolts on the cot sides until the whole cot is assembled, and never over-tighten them.
When fitting the top base position rails, make sure the pilot holes face upwards.
Keep unused fittings somewhere safe and out of children's reach, as you will need them for later stages.
Check and tighten all fittings every 2 to 3 weeks.
Clean with a damp cloth. Never use bleach or abrasive cleaners, as they damage the surface.
Once converted to a toddler or first bed, place it tight against a wall or leave a 300 mm gap, and keep it away from heaters, windows and other furniture.
Gaia Baby furniture has a 2 year warranty from the date of purchase. Register your product within 3 months of purchase and the warranty extends to 5 years.
Sizes
Length: 140 cm
Width: 70 cm
Height: 96 cm
Weight: 53.5 kg
Wood: Solid birch
Leg finish: Natural or Walnut
Mattress: Australian-made, included
Safe sleep
Always place your baby on their back to sleep on a firm, flat surface. Do not put objects or accessories in your baby's sleep space, and never place the cot near a blind, cord, strap or similar item that could wrap around a baby's neck. Use only one mattress in the cot.

articles.title: Gaia Baby Serena Mini Cot: wheels, mattress heights and extending to a cot bed
articles.text:
The Serena Mini Cot is a compact solid birch cot made for smaller rooms and for keeping your baby close in your bedroom. It comes with its own Australian-made mattress and suits babies from birth to around 2 years.
Mattress heights
Use the upper mattress position from birth. Once your baby can push up on their hands, roll over or pull up on the sides, usually at around 6 months, you must move the base to the lower position, and always before your baby can sit up unaided. The bottom base position is the safest position for the cot base. You can keep using the Mini Cot until your little one is around 2 years old.
Using the wheels
The Mini Cot can be fitted with either feet or lockable swivel castors, so it is easy to wheel from room to room.
To lock, push the locking tabs on the castors downwards until they lock with a click.
To unlock, push the locking tabs upwards until the castors release.
The Mini Cot is not designed for co-sleeping. It fits neatly beside your bed, but use it as a standalone cot.
Growing into a cot bed
When your baby outgrows the Mini Cot, the Serena Mini Cot Bed Extension (sold separately) grows the frame from about 90 cm to a 140 cm long cot bed. It includes extended side panels, side rails, a bed base and an Australian-made mattress, and lets you use the bed as a cot bed (2 to 3 years), toddler bed (3 to 4 years) and first bed (4 to 5 years).
Going the other way, the Serena Mini Cot Adaptor converts a Serena Convertible Cot Bed into the Mini Cot. It includes mini cot side panels, side rails, a bed base, wheels and an Australian-made mini cot mattress.

articles.title: Gaia Baby Serena Dresser: drawers, changing top and wall strap

Removing a drawer
Pull the drawer out as far as it will go.
Lift the locking catch on the left side upwards and push the locking catch on the right side downwards, and hold both in place.
With the catches held, slide the drawer runners off the arms of the dresser runners.
Refitting a drawer
Pull the arms on the dresser runners out as far as they will go.
Slide the arms onto the runners on the drawer sides until they lock in place with a click.
Push the drawer in until you feel pressure, then stop pushing. It will soft close by itself.

Wipe spills straight away and clean with a damp cloth. Never use abrasive cleaners or strong bleach.
To move the dresser, lift it with a second person. Never drag it.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey teethers: common questions
articles.text:
Ages, materials and how long to use your Matchstick Monkey teether.
About the teethers
What ages are the teethers suitable for?
All Matchstick Monkey teethers are tested for babies and toddlers from 3 months to 3 years.
What are the teethers made from? Are they BPA free?
Yes, they are BPA free. The teethers are made from high-quality, food-grade, non-toxic silicone.
What is BioCote?
BioCote is an antimicrobial technology built directly into the silicone during manufacturing, so it will not wear or wash away over time. It helps reduce microbes on the surface of the teether by up to 99.99% within 2 hours.
Using your teether
How long should I use my teether for?
For as long as your child is teething. Clean it regularly.
How do I clean my teether?
Each teether is a single piece of silicone, so it is easy to clean. Use a steam or cold water steriliser, boil it, or run it through the dishwasher.
Can I put it in the fridge or freezer?
The fridge is fine, and a cool teether can give extra relief on sore gums. Do not put teethers in the freezer, as frozen silicone can become too hard for tender gums.
Can I reuse my teether for a second child?
No. Matchstick Monkey does not recommend reusing a teether for another child. Teethers are chewed hard over months of use, so each child should start with their own.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey Original Teething Toy and Gel Applicator: how to use it
articles.text:
The Original Matchstick Monkey is a teething toy and a gel applicator in one. Here is how the textured bumps work and how to get the most out of it.
What the Original teether does
Each Original teether is one piece of food-grade, non-toxic, BPA-free silicone. The raised bumps on the back of the monkey's head massage tender gums, and the same bumps hold teething gel so it goes onto the gums rather than onto little fingers.
Textured bumps help massage sore gums, including the hard-to-reach back molars.
Easy-grip arms are shaped for little hands, so your baby can steer it themselves and build motor skills as they go.
It is flexible and lightweight, so it suits home, outings and travel.
It is tested for babies and toddlers from 3 months to 3 years.
Using the gel applicator
Squeeze a pea-sized amount of your usual teething gel onto the textured bumps on the back of the monkey's head.
Hand the teether to your baby. The easy-grip arms let them hold and position it on their own.
Let them chew. The bumps massage the gel onto sore gums, with no gel on fingers or faces.
Gel is optional. The textured bumps also massage tender gums on their own.
Cooling and cleaning
Pop the teether in the fridge for extra cooling relief, but never put it in the freezer, as frozen silicone is too hard for tender gums.
Clean it regularly in a steam or cold water steriliser, in boiling water or in the dishwasher. It is a single piece of silicone with no seams for grime to hide in.
Ages, materials and BioCote protection for every Matchstick Monkey teether are covered in our article Matchstick Monkey teethers: common questions.
Colours in the Australian range
The Original comes in 14 colours, so it is easy to tell teethers apart or match one to a pram or nappy bag.
Colours: Baby Blue, Blue, Confetti Cream, Dusty Pink, Emerald, Grey, Lilac, Mint Green, Olive, Orange, Peach, Pink, Red, Yellow
Material: Food-grade silicone with BioCote antimicrobial protection
Tested age: 3 months to 3 years
Fridge yes, freezer never
A cooled teether can soothe sore gums, but a frozen one is too hard for tender gums. Check the teether before each use and stop using it if it is damaged.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey animal teethers: Fox, Lion, Giraffe, Tiger, Pig, Shark and Dancing Monkey
articles.text:
The animal teethers work the same way as the Original monkey, with the same soothing bumps and easy grip, just with a different character on top.

Grip and textures
Every animal teether is designed to soothe sore gums and make teething easier for babies and toddlers.
Textured bumps massage tender gums and help apply teething gel more easily and hygienically, including harder-to-reach areas.
The lightweight, ergonomic shape is designed for little hands to grip, which also supports motor skill development.
They are flexible and lightweight, so they are practical at home, on outings and when travelling.
The Dancing Monkey has varied textures to massage tender gums and give sensory comfort during teething.
Using teething gel
Squeeze a pea-sized amount of your usual teething gel onto the textured bumps.
Hand the teether to your baby so they can hold it themselves.
Let them chew. The bumps help apply the gel to the gums.
Care and age
Animal teethers are made from the same food-grade, non-toxic, BPA-free silicone with BioCote antimicrobial protection as the Original, and are tested for babies and toddlers from 3 months to 3 years. They are cleaned and cooled the same way: steriliser, boiling water or dishwasher, and the fridge but never the freezer. See Matchstick Monkey teethers: common questions for more on care.
Original or animal?
Animal teethers and the Original monkey have the same soothing bumps and gel applicator. The Original comes in 14 colours, while the animal range adds a character.
One teether per child
Teethers are chewed hard over months of use, so we do not recommend passing one on to a second child. Check the teether before each use and stop using it if it is damaged.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey Teething Starter Set: what is in the box and how to use it
articles.text:

Each starter set includes:
A character teether (the animal teether) with textured bumps and easy-grip arms.
A flat teether for little hands.

Characters: Ludo Lion, Gigi Giraffe

Using the teethers

Hand it over. The easy-grip arms are shaped for little hands so your baby can steer it themselves.
Let them chew. The bumps massage sore gums, including hard-to-reach back molars.
The teethers help soothe sore gums, while the finger toothbrush supports gentle cleaning and gets babies used to brushing.

The teethers can go in the fridge for extra cooling relief, but never in the freezer.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey Baby Sonic Toothbrush: using it and changing the brush head
articles.text:
The Baby Sonic Toothbrush uses ultra-soft bristles and gentle sonic vibrations to make early brushing easier. Here is how to use it and keep it fresh.
Key features
Ultra-soft bristles for little teeth and gums.
Gentle sonic vibrations for early brushing routines.
A protective cap for hygienic storage and travel.
AAA battery included.
Five designs: Monkey, Dusty Pink, Ludo Lion, Gigi Giraffe and Teddy Tiger.
It is designed for early oral care once babies start getting their first teeth, usually around 6 months.
Brushing with it
Brush twice a day, morning and night, for about 2 minutes each time.
Use gentle circles over every tooth surface and let the sonic vibrations do the hard work.
Brush your own teeth at the same time and keep it light. Letting your toddler choose their own character helps too.
Rinse the brush and put the protective cap back on after each use.
Babies often chew the brush at first, which is normal. Let your baby hold it, but an adult should still finish the brushing.
Replacement heads
Replacement heads fit every Baby Sonic Toothbrush in the range.
When to replace: Every 3 months
Replace sooner if: The bristles splay or look worn or damaged
Compatible with: All Matchstick Monkey Baby Sonic Toothbrushes
First dental visit
Book your child's first dental visit when the first tooth appears or by their first birthday, whichever comes first.
Always supervise
Supervise your child whenever they hold the toothbrush and check the bristles regularly for wear or damage.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey brushing guide: when to start brushing your baby's teeth
articles.text:
Healthy oral care starts earlier than many parents expect. This guide covers the first steps, from cleaning gums to brushing first teeth.
Before the first tooth
You do not need a toothbrush yet. Wrap a clean, moist gauze pad or soft, damp washcloth around a clean finger and gently wipe along the gums. The aim is not to scrub, just to introduce gentle mouth care calmly.
From the first tooth
As soon as the first tooth appears, introduce a soft baby toothbrush. Brush twice a day, morning and night.
Choose a secure, comfortable position, such as your baby lying across your lap, or sitting or standing together in front of a mirror.
Use small, gentle movements rather than scrubbing.
Brush the front, back and chewing surfaces of every visible tooth, even if there is only one.
Smile, talk or sing while you brush to keep it positive.
Toothpaste
Current Australian guidance generally recommends a soft toothbrush and water only for babies up to 17 months, unless your dentist recommends toothpaste earlier. From 18 months to five years, a small pea-sized amount of low-fluoride toothpaste can generally be used twice a day. Encourage your child to spit it out rather than swallow it.
If you are unsure what is right for your child, ask your dentist, GP or maternal and child health nurse.
Making it easier
Let your baby hold a second toothbrush while you brush.
Brush your own teeth at the same time.
Sing the same short song each time.
Keep the routine short, calm and predictable.
If a session goes badly, simply try again at the next brushing time.
Chewing the toothbrush is normal while babies get used to it. Let them explore, but an adult should still do the brushing.
First dental visit
Arrange your child's first dental visit when their first tooth appears or by their first birthday, whichever comes first. This is general information only and does not replace advice from your dentist or health professional.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey Bath Time Boat Set and Bath Slide Set: play and care
articles.text:
Our two bath play sets are designed for splashing, sorting and exploring, and built without the squeeze holes that trap water in many bath toys.
What is in each set
Bath Time Boat Set: A boat and a wobbler
Boat Set colours: Red, Blue, Yellow
Bath Slide Set: One slide and three animal rocks
Designed for: Babies and toddlers, with adult supervision
Playing with them
Fix the slide to a smooth bath or tile surface, then let your child send the animal rocks down it.
Sorting the rocks onto the slide builds hand-eye coordination and fine motor skills.
The boat and wobbler encourage imaginative, sensory play and are easy for little hands to grasp.
Pouring and splashing builds wrist control and cause-and-effect thinking.
Water play helps set up the water confidence that swimming lessons build on.
Bath time is one of the few moments in the day when your baby has your full attention, warm water and nowhere else to be, which makes it a great time for play that builds real skills.
Keeping them mould free
The classic bath toy problem is a squeeze hole that traps water and grows mould you cannot see. These sets are made without squeeze holes or hidden chambers.
Rinse the toys after each bath.
Let them drain fully.
Leave them to dry completely before the next bath.
Do not leave them sitting in standing water between uses.
Supervise every bath
Active adult supervision at bath time, every time. Never leave a baby or toddler unattended in the bath, even for a moment, no matter how well the toys are designed.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey Hair Rinser: how to rinse hair without soap in the eyes
articles.text:
Hair washing can be the hardest part of bath time. The Hair Rinser is designed to keep soapy water away from little eyes so rinsing feels calmer.
How it works
A soft silicone lip sits comfortably against your child's head.
It offers two ways to pour: a gentle rainfall shower or a free-flow pour.
It is designed for babies and toddlers.
The open bowl dries fully between uses.
Pouring options: Gentle rainfall or free-flow pour
Lip: Soft silicone
Designed for: Babies and toddlers, with adult supervision
Rinsing step by step
Fill the rinser with water.
Rest the soft silicone lip snugly against your child's forehead.
Pour gently, using either the gentle rainfall or the free-flow pour, whichever your child finds most comfortable.
Keep the lip snug against the forehead while you pour to help keep soapy water away from little eyes.
After bath time
Rinse the Hair Rinser after each bath.
Let it drain and dry fully.
Do not leave it sitting in standing water between uses.
Used the same way each time, the rinser helps make hair washing a calmer part of the bath routine. Supervise your child the whole time and stop using the rinser if the silicone lip or body is damaged.
Supervise every bath
Never leave a baby or toddler unattended in the bath, even for a moment. Active adult supervision is needed at every bath time.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey teething guide: signs and stages month by month
articles.text:
Every baby teethes on their own schedule. This guide explains what is common at each stage and how a teether can help.
Early signs
Babies often start looking for pressure on their gums between about 3 and 6 months, sometimes weeks or months before a tooth appears. Common signs include:
Chewing fingers, hands and toys.
Increased drooling and flushed cheeks.
Rubbing their gums.
Wanting to bite during feeds.
Being a little fussier than usual.
Not every baby who chews is teething. Mouthing is also a normal way babies explore texture, shape and pressure.
When teeth commonly appear
Lower central incisors: 6 to 10 months
Upper central incisors: 8 to 12 months
Upper lateral incisors: 9 to 13 months
Lower lateral incisors: 10 to 16 months
First molars: 13 to 19 months
Canines: 16 to 23 months
Second molars: 23 to 33 months
By around age three, most children have all 20 baby teeth. Some babies cut their first tooth at four months, while others do not see one until after their first birthday, and both can be normal. This is a general guide, not a deadline.
How needs change
Babies may prefer a lightweight, easy-to-hold teether early on, slim textured surfaces for front teeth, and a design that reaches further back for molars. It is normal for a baby to reject a teether they used to like as different teeth come through.
When to see a health professional
Your baby seems unusually distressed for a long time.
You are worried about feeding or growth.
You notice significant swelling, bleeding or injury in the mouth.
Your child has no teeth well beyond the usual range and you are concerned.
Teething does not cause fever
A temperature of 38°C or higher is a fever and should not be put down to teething. This guide is general information only and does not replace advice from your GP, dentist or maternal and child health nurse.

articles.title: Matchstick Monkey teether safety: checking, replacing and keeping it off the floor
articles.text:
A teether spends a lot of time in your baby's mouth, so a quick check before each use matters. Here is what to look for and how to keep a teether close by.
Check before every use
Look over the whole teether for wear, cracking, splitting or any other damage.
Stop using it straight away if you find any damage, and replace it.
Always supervise your baby while they use a teether.
Use a separate teether for each child, as teethers are chewed hard over months of use.
Matchstick Monkey teethers are one piece of silicone with no seams or joins, which makes them easier to clean and inspect.
Keeping more than one
Many parents find more than one teether makes life easier, for example one at home, one in the nappy bag and one cooling in the fridge. Never put a teether in the freezer.
Using the Multi-Use Product Holder
The Multi-Use Product Holder is a silicone strap that keeps a teether, bottle or toy within reach and off the floor.
Adjust the strap to fit the teether, toy or bottle.
Attach it to a pram, highchair or car seat so the item stays within reach and off the floor.
Colours: Blue, Green, Pink, Yellow
Material: One piece of easy-clean silicone
Attaches to: Prams, highchairs, car seats and bags
If something is wrong on arrival
If your product arrives faulty, or you received the wrong item, let us know within 48 hours of receiving it. We will arrange a return authority, and please do not send anything back without one. Your rights under the Australian Consumer Law also apply.
Damaged means replace
If a teether shows any cracking, splitting or wear, stop using it and replace it. Do not freeze teethers and do not pass them on to another child.

articles.title: Using and cleaning your NoseFrida
articles.text:
The NoseFrida is a nasal aspirator you can use from birth. You create the suction yourself by breathing in through the mouthpiece, so you can feel the resistance and adjust it straight away. This guide covers how to use it, how to clean it and when to change the filter.
Before you start
Put a new hygiene filter into the filter chamber. The filter sits between the collection chamber and the mouthpiece and keeps mucus away from you.
Apply saline first. Put two to three drops in each nostril, then wait 20 to 30 seconds.
How to use it
Rest the large tube against the outside of one nostril so it forms a seal. The tube does not go inside the nose.
Breathe in steadily through the mouthpiece for two to three seconds while moving the tube in a small circle.
Repeat, then swap to the other nostril.
Many parents find it most helpful before feeds, before sleep and first thing in the morning.
Cleaning
After each session, throw the used filter away. Wash the parts in warm soapy water, or put them on the top rack of the dishwasher.
Filters
The NoseFrida itself is reusable. The filters are single use.
Use a fresh filter every time and bin it afterwards.
If suction feels weak, check the filter. A used or missing filter reduces suction.
Four filters come in the box. Replacement filters are sold separately in packs of 20. Use genuine Frida filters, which are sized for the NoseFrida chamber.
You may go through several filters in a day, so it helps to keep a spare pack in the change bag.
If you are worried about your baby
If you have any concerns about your baby's breathing, feeding or health, see your doctor or child health nurse.
Need more help?
If a part is missing or something is not working as it should, send us a request and our Melbourne team will help.
Get help with a product

articles.title: How to use your Frida Mom postpartum products
articles.text:
The Frida Mom postpartum products are designed to be used together as a simple bathroom routine after birth. All of these items are for external use.
The routine
Cleanse with the Peri Bottle. Fill it with warm water before you sit down. Hold it upside down and spray from front to back while you are on the toilet and afterwards, then pat dry.
Wear the disposable underwear. It holds a maxi pad and an ice pad in place. It is single use, so bin it after wearing.
Cool with an Instant Ice Maxi Pad. Fold the pad in half to activate it, then shake. Place it in your underwear and wear it for up to 20 minutes at a time. No freezer is needed. Each pad is single use. After a caesarean, only use the cooling near your incision if your midwife has said so.
Add a Cooling Pad Liner. Lay a liner on top of your maternity pad, front to back. Replace it every time you change your pad.
Finish with Perineal Foam. Shake the bottle, then pump the foam onto your pad or liner. You can use it at every pad change.
Looking after the Peri Bottle
Rinse the bottle and let it air dry between uses. Refill it so it is ready for your next bathroom visit.
Choosing your underwear
The High Waist style has a waistband that sits above a caesarean incision.
The Boyshort style has a lower rise and feels more like everyday underwear.
Both styles are one size fits most.
Which kit has the Peri Bottle?
The Postpartum Recovery Kit does not include the Peri Bottle. The Hospital Labour and Delivery Kit does, along with a gown, socks and a carry bag. The bottle is also sold separately.
If you are worried
If you have any concerns about your recovery, speak to your doctor, midwife or child health nurse.
Need more help?
If something is missing or not working as it should, send us a request and our Melbourne team will help.
