articles.title: Frida Baby MediFrida: how to give medicine and clean the dispenser
articles.text:
The MediFrida is a medicine dispenser shaped like a dummy. Your baby sucks as they would on a dummy while you press the syringe, so the medicine goes to the inside of the cheek rather than the back of the throat.
What is in the box
One MediFrida dummy dispenser.
One dosing syringe.
One 5 ml measuring cup.
How to give a dose
Confirm the dose with your pharmacist or GP before you start.
Draw the dose into the supplied syringe, or any standard oral syringe, and check the markings twice.
Push the syringe into the side channel of the dummy with a slight twist until it sits firmly.
Offer the dummy as you normally would. Once your baby is sucking, press the plunger slowly.
Keep the dummy in for a few more sucks, then remove the syringe and close the tab. The MediFrida then works as an ordinary dummy while your baby settles.
Getting the full dose
About 0.2 ml of medicine can stay inside the dummy channel after dosing. For doses over 1 ml that is a small share. For very small doses, under 1 ml, such as vitamin D drops, ask your pharmacist how to load the syringe to allow for it.
It suits liquid medicines given by oral syringe, such as children's paracetamol and ibuprofen, liquid antibiotics, vitamin drops and gripe water.
Thick suspensions are not suitable, as they can block the channel.
If your baby will not take it, an oral syringe aimed at the inside of the cheek does the same job.
Cleaning
Take it apart straight after use and rinse in warm water.
The dummy and the syringe are both top-rack dishwasher safe.
Never leave medicine to dry in the channel.
Age and dosing
The MediFrida can be used from birth, but dose accuracy matters most for newborns, so check with your pharmacist before the first use. It is not recommended for children over three. It is a delivery tool, not a medicine: the dose, the timing and whether to give medicine at all are for your pharmacist or GP to advise.

articles.title: Frida Baby SnipperClipper Set: how to cut your baby's nails safely
articles.text:
The SnipperClipper Set is a baby nail clipper with a spyhole window above the blades and a guard that keeps the blade away from the fingertip, plus a file for smoothing the edges. It is designed for use from birth through toddlerhood.
What is in the set
The SnipperClipper nail clipper with spyhole and guard, with curved, nickel-free stainless steel blades.
A curved S-shaped baby nail file.
A storage case.
How to cut your baby's nails
Choose the moment: deep sleep after a feed, or straight after a warm bath when nails are soft. Avoid times when your baby is hungry, tired or has just woken with a startle.
Hold the finger between your thumb and forefinger and press the pad of the fingertip down, away from the nail.
Look through the spyhole. It shows how much nail is in the cutting mouth and whether any skin is, so adjust before you squeeze.
Snip in small sections along the natural curve of the nail. One or two small snips is usually enough. Leave a sliver of white.
Smooth the edges with the S-file so there are no sharp corners.
How often to trim
Many Australian nurses suggest filing only for the first two to four weeks, while newborn nails are paper-soft and close to the skin. If your newborn is scratching, file first.
Newborn, 0 to 3 months: File only for the first two to four weeks, then clip fingernails every one to two weeks and toenails every three to four weeks
3 to 12 months: Fingernails every one to two weeks, toenails every three to four weeks
Toddler: Fingernails every one to two weeks, toenails every two to three weeks
Care
Rinse and dry the clipper and file after use.
Keep them in the storage case between uses.
Toenails are thicker and grow more slowly, and the clipper copes with them too.
If you nick a fingertip
Press gently with a clean cloth for a minute. Do not put a plaster on a baby's finger, as it is a choking hazard. It happens to most parents once and usually heals quickly. See your GP if the bleeding will not stop.

articles.title: Frida Baby 3-in-1 Nose, Nail and Ear Picker: which tip does what
articles.text:
The 3-in-1 Picker is a small grooming tool for dried mucus at the nostril opening, grit under tiny nails and visible wax at the outer ear. Every tip has a stopper so it cannot go too deep, and it is suitable from the newborn stage through toddlerhood.
What each tip is for
Nose tip: lifts dried, crusty mucus from just inside the nostril opening, the bits the NoseFrida cannot move.
Nail tip: cleans lint, milk and general grit from under tiny nails.
Ear tip: clears visible wax from the outer ear only.
Utility tip: for belly button fluff, neck rolls and between the toes.
The tips click into the handle. Use each tip only for its own job.
How to use it
Choose the tip you need and click it onto the handle.
Use it after a warm bath if you can. Steam softens dried mucus and wax so it lifts more easily.
Rest your hand against your baby's cheek to steady the head, so the picker moves with them if they turn.
Scoop gently outward with a light touch. If something does not come away easily, leave it for another day.
Wash the tips, dry them and put everything back in the case.
Picker or NoseFrida?
The NoseFrida uses suction for wet, runny mucus during a cold, with saline first. The Picker is for dry, crusty bits at the nostril opening, especially once a cold has passed. Many families use both.
Cleaning and storage
Rinse the tips in warm soapy water after each use and let them air dry.
Check the tips for wear before each use.
Store everything in the case so the right tip is easy to find.
Outer ear only
The ear tip is for visible wax at the outer ear only. Never put it inside the ear canal. Cotton buds are not recommended for a baby's ears or nose, as they push wax and mucus further in. A smelly ear, discharge or signs of ear pain need a GP, not a tool.

articles.title: Frida Baby Flake Fixer: using the three-step cradle cap kit
articles.text:
Cradle cap is a build-up of yellowish, greasy flakes on a baby's scalp in the first months. It is very common, not itchy and not contagious, and it usually clears on its own. The Flake Fixer helps keep it tidy in the meantime with three gentle steps in the bath.
What is in the box
One sponge.
One silicone brush.
One fine-tooth comb.
How to use it in the bath
Lather: wet the sponge and work a little baby wash into the scalp.
Loosen: brush in small circles with the silicone brush.
Lift: comb through gently with the fine-tooth comb to remove the loosened flakes.
Rinse your baby's scalp well.
How often and where
Use it a couple of times a week in the bath, not every night. Over-scrubbing can irritate the scalp.
Cradle cap can also appear on the eyebrows. Use only the soft sponge and brush there, very gently, and keep them away from the eyes.
Cleaning
Rinse all three parts after use and let them dry.
All three parts are dishwasher safe.
When to see someone
If the scalp is red, weeping, spreading to the body or not improving after a few weeks, see your GP or child health nurse.

articles.title: Frida Baby Skinsoother: using the silicone bath brush for cradle cap and dry skin
articles.text:
The Skinsoother is a soft silicone brush that fits in your palm. It gently lifts loose flakes in the bath, and its raised massage beads help work moisturiser into the skin afterwards. It is suitable from birth.
Using it for cradle cap
Massage a little coconut, olive or baby oil into the scalp 10 to 15 minutes before the bath to soften the flakes.
In lukewarm water, brush in slow, small circles over the scalp with a gentle baby wash. Hot water dries skin further.
Rinse well and pat dry. Do not rub, and do not chase every flake in one bath.
While the skin is still damp, apply your usual baby moisturiser and use the raised beads to work it in.
Rinse the brush and press its suction cup onto the bath wall so it dries between uses.
Dry patches and everyday bathing
Two or three times a week is enough for cradle cap.
For dry patches on the cheeks, scalp and creases, brush gently at bath time, then moisturise while the skin is damp.
It can be used very gently on the face. Keep it away from the eyes.
On the scalp, including the soft spot, use light pressure only.
For thick or widespread cradle cap, the Flake Fixer kit adds a fine-tooth comb.
In the box and care
One Skinsoother silicone brush and a suction cup for storing it on the bath wall.
BPA-free and phthalate-free.
Rinse and air-dry after each use. It is also dishwasher safe.
When to see someone
If the skin is red, weeping, cracked or not improving after a few weeks, see your GP or child health nurse. Eczema and skin infections need a proper check, not a brush.

articles.title: Frida Baby Fingerbrush and ToothHugger: cleaning gums and first teeth
articles.text:
The Fingerbrush slips over your finger for cleaning gums and first teeth from birth. The ToothHugger is a toddler toothbrush with a U-shaped head that cleans the front, back and biting surface of each tooth in one pass.
Which brush when
Birth to 6 months: Fingerbrush and water on the gums after feeds
6 to 18 months: Fingerbrush on the gums and first teeth
From about 18 months: ToothHugger, when there are enough teeth and your toddler wants to hold the brush
Many families use both for a while during the changeover.
Using the Fingerbrush
Wash your hands.
Slip the Fingerbrush over your index finger, textured side out. It fits snugly and protects your finger if your baby bites down.
Use water alone for gums and for babies under 18 months.
Brush in small circles along the front and back gums and any teeth that have come through. Thirty seconds is plenty.
Rinse in warm water and store it in its stand with the lid on.
Using the ToothHugger
Add a smear of low-fluoride children's toothpaste, not adult toothpaste.
Let your toddler have a go first to build the habit.
Then you finish: guide the head over each tooth with gentle pressure.
Brush twice a day, in the morning and last thing at night. Spit, do not rinse.
Rinse the brush and stand it upright on its suction base, bristles up.
Care and replacement
Fingerbrush: rinse after each use, or wash with mild soap and air dry. It is dishwasher safe. Replace it if the bristles wear or tear.
ToothHugger: replace it every three months, sooner if the blue indicator bristles have faded to white or the bristles have splayed, and after an illness.
Both are BPA-free and latex-free.
Good to know
The Australian Dental Association recommends cleaning a baby's gums before any teeth appear, brushing twice a day from the first tooth, using a smear of low-fluoride children's toothpaste from 18 months, and a first dental check by the first birthday. Until about age seven or eight, a parent should do the effective brushing. Ask your dentist or child health nurse about anything specific to your child.

articles.title: Frida Mom Labour & Delivery Kit and Postpartum Recovery Kit: what is in each
articles.text:
Frida Mom makes two kits. The Postpartum Recovery Kit holds the bathroom essentials for the first days after birth, and the Hospital Labour & Delivery Kit includes everything in the Recovery Kit plus the items for labour and the hospital bag.
What is in each kit
Disposable underwear: 4 pairs, in both kits
Instant Ice Maxi Pads: 4 pads, in both kits
Witch hazel cooling pad liners: In both kits
Perineal Foam: In both kits
Bathroom caddy: In both kits
Upside Down Peri Bottle: Labour & Delivery Kit only
Labour & Delivery Gown: Labour & Delivery Kit only
Labour socks: Labour & Delivery Kit only
Toiletry carry bag: Labour & Delivery Kit only
The gown and socks
The gown has snap closures at the shoulders so midwives have monitoring access, with full coverage at the back.
The front opens for skin-to-skin contact and breastfeeding after birth.
It has pockets for a phone and lip balm.
It is 100% viscose (bamboo-derived). One size fits XS to XL, with room for late pregnancy.
The labour socks are warm and non-slip for moving around during labour.
How the kit is used
Labour: gown and socks on (Labour & Delivery Kit).
Straight after birth: bend an Instant Ice Maxi Pad to activate it and place it in the disposable underwear.
First bathroom visit: rinse with warm water, place a liner on the pad and add Perineal Foam to the liner. The peri bottle is in the Labour & Delivery Kit or sold separately.
Hospital stay: sit the caddy on the toilet cistern so everything is within reach.
At home: move the caddy home and continue the same routine.
When to order and topping up
Order by 36 weeks so the kit is ready to pack with your hospital bag. Both kits suit recovery after a vaginal birth or a caesarean. The kits cover the hospital stay and the first days at home, and extra underwear, ice pads and liners are sold separately.
Good to know
The ice pads, liners, foam and peri bottle are for external use only. Discuss your labour, birth and recovery plan with your midwife, obstetrician or GP.

articles.title: Frida Mom disposable postpartum underwear: sizing and which cut to choose
articles.text:
Frida Mom disposable postpartum underwear comes in two cuts, High Waist and Boyshort, in one stretchy size. Both hold a maternity pad, cooling liner or Instant Ice Maxi Pad in place and are worn once, then binned.
High Waist or Boyshort?
High Waist: a taller band that sits above a caesarean incision from day one. Also fine after a vaginal birth if you prefer more coverage, and the more versatile choice if you are unsure.
Boyshort: sits at the natural waist with a wider leg, below a caesarean incision line. The everyday cut for vaginal birth recovery, or for anyone who prefers a lower rise.
Size guide
One size: Medium/Large. The waistband stretches from 71 cm to 107 cm (28 to 42 inches).
AU 8: 66 cm waist (26 in): roomy
AU 10: 71 cm (28 in): comfortable
AU 12: 76 cm (30 in): comfortable
AU 14: 81 cm (32 in): comfortable
AU 16: 86 cm (34 in): comfortable
AU 18: 91 cm (36 in): comfortable
AU 20: 96 cm (38 in): good fit
AU 22: 102 cm (40 in): snug, top of range
AU 24: 107 cm (42 in): at stretch limit
How to measure
Measure around your waist where the band will sit.
For the High Waist cut, postpartum that is usually up near the belly button rather than your natural waist.
For the Boyshort, measure at your natural waist.
Your belly is larger than your usual waist in the early weeks and you will be wearing a pad, so allow a little extra room. AU dress sizes are a guide only.
Wearing them
Put the maternity pad, cooling liner or Instant Ice Maxi Pad inside the underwear before you pull them on.
Pull them on gently. They are four-way stretch microfibre and spandex, with no seams or tags.
Change them with the pad: wear once, then bin.
Expect two to four changes a day in the first 48 hours, then fewer. A pack of eight covers two to four days of the heaviest bleeding, so many mums buy two packs. They also work for heavy periods later on.

articles.title: Setting up and using your Hannie Portable High Chair
articles.text:
Your Hannie Portable High Chair straps onto a dining chair you already own, so your child can sit up at the table with the family. This guide covers which chairs suit it, the age and weight limits, and how to pack it for travel.
Check the dining chair first
Attach the seat only to a sturdy chair with four legs, a firm, flat seat and a high backrest. The chair needs to measure at least:
Seat width: 38 cm
Seat depth: 35 cm
Backrest height: 30 cm
Do not use stools, backless benches, swivel, rocking or folding chairs, soft or deeply padded seats, or any chair that is wobbly, damaged or lightweight.
Age and weight limits
Suitable from around 6 months, once your baby has good head and neck control and can sit upright without help, up to around 5 years.
Baby Chair mode (with the harness, used with or without the tray and Reversible Cushion): up to 36 months or 15 kg, whichever comes first.
Toddler Seat mode: from 3 to 5 years, up to 25 kg.
The Reversible Cushion and its Back Plate Support give younger babies extra comfort and stability. You can remove the cushion as your child grows.
Safety every time
Read the manual before first use and keep it handy.
Always fit the 3-point harness.
Check that both straps are tight before every meal.
Supervise your child during use and never leave them unattended.
Never use the seat freestanding on the floor, on a table, or in wet environments.
Folding and carrying
The seat folds flat and slips into the tote bag that comes with it. Packed, it weighs about 2 kg including the Reversible Cushion, and it fits under most pram baskets.

articles.title: Cleaning and caring for your Hannie Portable High Chair
articles.text:
Mealtimes are messy, so your Hannie Portable High Chair is made to be cleaned easily. Each part has its own care method, so follow the steps below to keep everything in good condition.
Tray
The tray is food-safe and dishwasher-safe. Use a gentle cycle at 50 to 60°C.
For a quick clean, wipe it with a damp cloth instead.
Seat and seat support
Wipe the seat and seat support with a damp cloth after meals.
For stubborn stains, use warm water and a mild detergent.
Do not put the seat or seat support in the dishwasher.
Reversible Cushion
Remove the Back Plate Support before washing.
Machine wash on a gentle cycle at up to 40°C.
Tumble dry on low.
Do not dry clean.
Harness
Machine wash at 40°C inside a laundry bag.
Do not tumble dry the harness.
Looking after your seat
The seat is designed to attach to a dining chair only, and it should never be used in wet environments. Your user manual has the full care instructions, and following them helps keep your warranty valid. Normal wear and tear, including changes in colour or surface finish, and damage from sun, heat, moisture or humidity are not covered by the warranty.
When you put the seat back together after cleaning, refit the 3-point harness and check that both straps are tight before the next meal.

articles.title: Hannie Portable High Chair fit guide: which dining chairs work and how to measure
articles.text:
The Hannie attaches to most standard dining chairs, but not to every chair. A tape measure and a couple of minutes will tell you whether yours is suitable.
The minimum chair sizes
The user manual sets out the minimum size of adult chair the Hannie can be used on, and the chair also needs to be the right type. Check all of these:
Seat width: At least 38 cm, side to side at the widest usable point
Seat depth: At least 35 cm, from the front edge to the backrest
Backrest height: At least 30 cm, from the seat surface to the top of the backrest
Legs: Four legs (not a stool or pedestal base)
Seat surface: Firm and flat, not soft or padded
Movement: Does not swivel, fold or rock
How to measure your chair
Measure the seat from side to side at its widest usable point. It needs to be at least 38 cm.
Measure the seat depth from the front edge of the seat to the backrest. It needs to be at least 35 cm.
Measure the backrest from the seat surface to the top of the backrest. It needs to be at least 30 cm.
Check the chair has four legs and a firm, flat seat, and that it does not swivel, fold or rock.
If you would like a second opinion, enter your measurements in the interactive fit guide on the Hannie website for an answer in seconds.
Chairs that work and chairs to skip
These chairs usually work well:
Solid timber dining chairs.
Sturdy café-style chairs with firm seats.
Chairs with a high, supportive backrest.
Most standard four-leg kitchen chairs.
Do not attach the Hannie to any of these:
Bar stools and backless benches.
Swivel, rocking or folding chairs.
Deeply padded or sprung seats.
Anything wobbly, damaged or lightweight.
Positioning the seat on the chair
Centre the seat on the adult chair, leaving at least 1 cm of chair seat clear on each side.
Click and fasten the wide strap under the adult seat first, then click the narrow strap around the backrest.
Make sure the rubber feet under the seat are sitting on the chair and working as contact points.
Check both straps are tight before every use.
Place the chair so your child cannot push their feet against the table or anything else, as this can tip the chair over.
The setup film on the Hannie how-to videos page shows the whole process from start to finish.
Only ever on an adult dining chair
The Hannie is designed only to be attached to a suitable adult dining chair. Never use it freestanding on the floor, on a table, in the bath or anywhere wet, and never leave your child unattended.

articles.title: Hannie Portable High Chair: Baby Chair mode, Toddler Seat mode and growing with your child
articles.text:
The Hannie is designed to be the one seat your child uses at the table from around 6 months to around 5 years. It changes with them as you add or remove parts, so there is no new chair to buy.
The two modes at a glance
Baby Chair mode: The seat with the 3-point harness, used with or without the tray and the Reversible Cushion with Back Plate Support
Baby Chair mode limit: Up to 36 months or 15 kg, whichever comes first
Toddler Seat mode: The seat used at booster height, with the cushion removed
Toddler Seat mode limit: From 3 to 5 years, up to 25 kg
Overall age range: Around 6 months to around 5 years
Four seating options
The user manual shows four ways to use the seat. When you are not using a part, it stores inside the seat compartment.
Baby Chair with tray.
Baby Chair.
Baby Chair without the cushion.
Toddler Seat.
How the seat changes as your child grows
Around 6 months: first tastes in Baby Chair mode, with the cushion, Back Plate Support, harness and tray.
From 7 to 9 months: finger foods and plenty of mess. The tray wipes down or goes in the dishwasher.
Around 12 months: spoon experiments begin, in the same seat with the same routine.
Around 18 months: many toddlers want to eat with the family, so take the tray off and pull the chair up to the table.
From 3 years: Toddler Seat mode, with the cushion retired and the seat at booster height, rated to 25 kg.
To 5 years: your child keeps their own seat at home, at cafés and at the grandparents' place.
When to start and when to switch
Start from around 6 months, once your baby has steady head and neck control and can sit upright without help. Every baby moves at their own pace, and your child health nurse or GP is the right person to ask if you are unsure.
The user manual gives Baby Chair mode as suitable up to 36 months or a maximum of 15 kg, and Toddler Seat mode from 3 to 5 years, up to 25 kg. Whichever of these your child reaches first, 36 months or 15 kg, is the time to move on from Baby Chair mode.
As your child grows, you simply remove the cushion. The Hannie Learning Hub has a stage-by-stage guide to the first five years at the table.
Weight limits
Never go over 15 kg in Baby Chair mode or 25 kg in Toddler Seat mode. Damage caused by overloading, including going over the stated weight limits, is not covered by the warranty.

articles.title: Hannie 3-point safety harness and Reversible Cushion: fitting them correctly
articles.text:
The Reversible Cushion and the 3-point safety harness work together in Baby Chair mode. The cushion gives a younger baby comfort and support, and the harness keeps them safely in the seat.
What the cushion and Back Plate Support do
The Reversible Cushion is designed for the youngest users, giving extra comfort while they learn to sit and find their balance.
The Back Plate Support sits in a pocket inside the cushion and adds ergonomic support and stability while your baby is still learning to sit through a meal.
The user manual notes that the Back Plate Support adds 7 cm in height.
The cushion is reversible, so you choose which side faces up.
As your child grows, you simply remove the cushion.
Unfolding the cushion
Undo the double buttons to release the strap.
Unfold the cushion, making sure the Back Plate Support is securely in its pocket.
Line up the double buttons correctly and snap them together to secure the Back Plate Support.
Fitting the cushion and harness to the seat
When you fit the seat support, thread the strap on the cushion around the fasteners on the seat support to hold the cushion in place.
Choose which side of the cushion you want facing up and find the three openings.
Thread the three harness straps through the openings.
Click the side straps into the buckle on the centre strap.
Strapping your child in
Pull the waist straps over your child's thighs, making sure they lie flat.
Fasten the waist straps snugly around the waist, connecting them to the strap between the legs.
Check that all three straps are snug but not too tight.
The how-to videos on the Hannie website include a short film on fitting the 3-point harness and Reversible Cushion.
Harness on, every time
Use the harness for every meal and snack, however short. The tray is not designed to hold your child in the seat. Until your child can get in and out of the seat without help, at about two and a half years, they must be secured with the harness at all times.

articles.title: Hannie Portable High Chair tray: fitting, removing and using it as a lid
articles.text:
The tray gives your child their own food-safe eating surface wherever you are, and when you pack up, it clicks over the seat compartment as a lid.
Fitting the tray
Slide the two circles on the tray down into the round openings on the seat support, and check they have snapped in correctly.
Rotate the tray down. The hook on the underside must snap over the edge of the seat support.
Push the tray down firmly until it clicks, then check it is properly fixed.
Removing the tray
Hold the tray and pull it towards you so it detaches from the seat support.
Keep holding it as you lift the tray upwards.
Release your grip and press in the two circles so they come free of the seat support.
When you unpack the chair, turn it so the bottom side faces up, then pull the tray upwards to detach it.
Using the tray as a lid
Once the seat support, straps, buckles and cushion are stored in the seat compartment, the tray closes it like a lid.
Position the tray above the compartment, tilting the front side down so it fits into the slots. This step is important for a proper fit.
Press down until you hear a click.
Pick it up and you are ready to go.
Good to know
The tray is food-safe and dishwasher-safe on a gentle cycle at 50 to 60°C, or you can wipe it with a damp cloth.
Around 18 months, many toddlers are ready to eat from the family table, so you can take the tray off and pull the chair up to the table.
Because it is your child's own surface, the tray works the same at a café, on holiday or at the grandparents' place.
The tray is not a restraint, so always fasten the 3-point harness as well.
The tray does not hold your child in
The tray is not designed to keep your child in the seat. Always fasten the 3-point harness and keep an adult within arm's reach.

articles.title: Travelling with the Hannie Portable High Chair: packing, cafés and holidays
articles.text:
Packed in its tote, the Hannie weighs about 2 kg including the cushion and fits under most pram baskets, so any venue with ordinary dining chairs can become baby-friendly.
Packing it up
Remove the tray: pull it towards you, lift it upwards and press in the two circles to free it from the seat support.
Press both sides of the front buckle at once to release it.
Press both sides of the seat support in opposite directions to disconnect it, then lift it up and off the seat.
Tilt the seat support so its front end sits beneath the front edge of the seat.
Place all the straps and buckles in the seat compartment.
Place the cushion in the seat compartment last.
Tilt the front of the tray down into the slots above the compartment and press until it clicks.
Slip the packed chair into its protective tote bag.
The Grab and go film on the how-to videos page shows the whole packing routine.
Where it earns its keep
Cafés and restaurants: attach it to a standard dining chair in under a minute, so your baby sits at the table in a seat they already know.
Holidays: a 2 kg chair in the boot means you are not relying on your accommodation having a high chair.
The grandparents' place: rather than buying a second high chair, the seat travels with your baby.
Out with the pram: packed in its tote, it fits under most pram baskets.
A simple eating-out kit
The Hannie in its tote, under the pram.
Two bibs, one for the meal and one for the ride home.
A damp cloth in a zip bag, because the tray wipes clean but faces do not.
A few familiar foods, even if you are ordering for them.
Check the chair wherever you go
Café and holiday rental chairs vary. Before you attach the seat, check the chair has four legs, a firm flat seat at least 38 cm wide and 35 cm deep, and a backrest at least 30 cm high. Skip bar stools, benches, and swivel, folding, rocking or padded chairs. The rules from home travel with the seat: harness clipped every time and an adult within arm's reach.
Not for cars, and not for carrying your child
Never use the Hannie in a motor vehicle, and never lift or carry your child while they are in the seat. Damage that happens during transport, including when the chair travels as luggage, is not covered by the warranty.

articles.title: Hannie Portable High Chair safety: standards, warnings and everyday habits
articles.text:
The Hannie is tested to the standard written for chair-mounted seats, but no seat is safe by certificate alone. How it is used matters just as much, at home and out.
What the standards mean
EN 16120:2012+A2:2017 is the European standard for chair-mounted seats. It covers structural strength, the attachment system, restraint requirements and stability.
AS/NZS 8124.3 is the Australian and New Zealand standard that limits the migration of certain elements from materials children may put in their mouths.
CPN No. 11 and US FDA 21 CFR add US consumer product and food-contact material requirements, which matter for a tray that children touch and mouth constantly.
Five everyday habits
Harness on every time, even for a 90-second snack.
The right chair underneath: sturdy, four legs, a firm flat seat at least 38 by 35 cm and a backrest at least 30 cm high.
Attach the seat exactly as the manual shows and check both straps are tight before every use.
An adult within arm's reach, always.
Respect the limits: 15 kg in Baby Chair mode and 25 kg in Toddler Seat mode.
Warnings from the user manual
Always use the chair attachment system and the restraint system, and check both are fitted correctly before use.
Check the seat is secure and stable on the adult chair before every use, and that the rubber feet are working as contact points.
Only use the seat for children who can sit upright without help.
Position the chair so your child cannot push their feet against the table or any other structure, as this can tip the chair over.
Never let your child push away from the table.
Never lift and carry your child in the seat.
Never use the seat in a motor vehicle.
Do not use the seat if any part is missing, torn or broken.
Only use accessories and replacement parts approved by the manufacturer.
Out and about
Café high chairs can be missing harnesses or be damaged. Bringing your own seat means the set-up at a restaurant is the same as at home: the same harness, the same fit rules and the same familiar seat.
Why the harness matters
The user manual warns that children have suffered head injuries, including skull fractures, after falling with or from booster seats. Never leave your child unattended, and never use the seat freestanding on the floor, on a table or in wet places.

articles.title: Hannie Portable High Chair colours, materials and specifications
articles.text:
Every Hannie Portable High Chair has the same design, parts and limits. The only difference between them is the colour you choose.
The four colours
White Sand.
Sage Green.
Charcoal Black.
Mahogany Red.
Each colour has its own product page on the Hannie website, and each comes complete with the seat, frame, Reversible Cushion with Back Plate Support, 3-point harness, tray and protective tote bag. There is nothing extra to buy.
Materials
Product materials: Polypropylene (PP), TPE, polyester and polyamide (PA)
Cushion outer: 100% polyester
Cushion filling: 50% polyester, 50% polyurethane
Tray: Food-safe and dishwasher-safe
End of life: 100% recyclable by the end user
Size, weight and standards
Height: 277 mm
Width: 352 mm
Length: 344 mm
Product weight: 1.8 kg
Packed weight: About 2 kg including the Reversible Cushion
Baby Chair mode: Up to 36 months or 15 kg
Toddler Seat mode: 3 to 5 years, up to 25 kg
Minimum dining chair: Seat 38 cm wide and 35 cm deep, backrest at least 30 cm
Safety standards: EN 16120:2012+A2:2017, AS/NZS 8124.3, CPN No. 11, US FDA 21 CFR
Colour, finish and wear
Normal wear and tear, including changes in colour or surface finish over time, is not covered by the warranty.
Minor material or colour variations between components are not covered by the warranty.
Damage caused by sun exposure, heat, moisture, humidity or pollution is not covered by the warranty.
Check the chair regularly for damage, and repair or replace parts promptly with Hannie-recommended parts.

articles.title: Hannie Portable High Chair warranty: what is covered and how to make a claim
articles.text:
Hannie products bought in Australia come with a 2-year warranty from the original date of purchase. In Australia, all warranty claims and support are handled by Coolkidz Australia, the exclusive authorised distributor of Hannie.
What the warranty covers
The warranty covers manufacturing faults under normal use. It applies where:
The product has been used under normal conditions and only for its intended purpose.
It has been maintained as the user manual describes.
A valid, dated proof of purchase is provided.
The product is presented in its original condition.
Only genuine Hannie parts have been used, and any modifications have prior written approval.
This warranty is in addition to your rights under Australian Consumer Law, which cannot be excluded.
What it does not cover
Normal wear and tear, including changes in colour or surface finish.
Minor material or colour variations between components.
Damage from sun exposure, heat, moisture, humidity or pollution.
Damage from accidents, impact, tipping, misuse or overloading, including going over the stated weight limits.
Damage during transport, including when the product travels as luggage.
Consequential or indirect loss or damage, including injury to people or damage to other property.
Use of accessories or components not supplied or approved by Hannie.
Second-hand owners
The warranty stays valid for second-hand owners for the rest of the 2 years from the original purchase date, as long as the original proof of purchase is supplied. It is one of the reasons the Hannie is easy to hand down to a sibling or sell on.
How to make a claim
Send us a request with your proof of purchase, such as a receipt or order number.
Include a detailed description of the issue.
Add clear photos or videos showing the fault.
If your claim is approved, we will send you return instructions.
Once we receive the product, we inspect it to confirm the issue is covered and arrange a remedy.
If the fault is covered, Coolkidz Australia will, at its discretion, repair the product at no cost. If repair is not possible, it will replace it with the same or an equivalent model, and if neither is feasible, refund the purchase price to the original payment method. In some cases store credit or a discount may be offered instead.
Keep your proof of purchase
A valid, dated proof of purchase is needed for every claim, whether you bought the chair new or second-hand. Keep the receipt or order confirmation for the full 2 years.

articles.title: Setting up and using your Magic nappy bin
articles.text:
Magic nappy bins do not use refill cartridges. Every bin in the range works the same way: you drop the nappy in, turn the top, and a wave seal closes behind it. Here is how to set yours up and use it day to day.
Know your model
Heka M, Heka L and Thoth L are telescopic, so they can extend in height when you need more room.
Majestic is a fixed-height bin.
Fitting a bag (Heka and Thoth)
Lift the lid off and place a bag into the holder.
Tuck the top of the bag under the rim so the seal can close over it.
Put the lid back on until it clicks.
Every nappy change
On a Heka or Thoth, drop the nappy into the opening and turn the top. The drum moves the nappy into the sealed part of the bin. Always return the top to its resting position afterwards.
On a Majestic, drop the nappy into the opening, then turn the handle forward and back. Leave the bin in the stand-by position, with the cup open, so no smell escapes.
Making more room
On a Heka or Thoth, twist the base to extend the bin. You can collapse it again for storage or travel.
Changing the bag
Press the small button on the side to release the top. The top is designed to stay locked until you do this, even when the bag is full.
Lift the whole top section off together with the bag.
Twist the bag a few times to seal it.
On a Heka or Thoth, tie the bag and lift it out. On a Majestic, tear the bag from the holder. Put it out with your usual rubbish.
Fit a new bag.

articles.title: Cleaning and odour tips for your Magic nappy bin
articles.text:
When a Magic nappy bin is used correctly it should not let odours out. If yours has started to smell, the cause is usually the bag, the lid, or the position the bin is left in between changes. Work through these checks first.
Check the bag
Make sure the bag is fitted correctly and has no holes or tears.
Most plastic bags and standard bin liners will work, but better quality bags give better results.
Avoid very thin supermarket shopping bags, as they may not seal properly.
Magic nappy bags are made to fit the bin and are designed to help lock in odours for up to two weeks when used correctly.
Check the lid and position
Close the top lid properly after every use.
Leave the opening in the stand-by position, with the cup open and not with the rounded side facing up.
Check that the bin itself is closed securely.
How to clean your bin
Unscrew the drum holder, as shown in your manual, and take out the round drum.
Wash all parts by hand in lukewarm water with a few tablespoons of baking soda and a little mild soap.
Rinse everything well.
Let every part air dry completely before you put the bin back together.
Do not put any part of the bin in the dishwasher.
Bag safety
Keep plastic bags away from children, and store bag rolls somewhere locked or out of reach.
Still noticing a smell?
If the odour continues after these checks and a full clean, send us a request and our Melbourne team will help.
Get help with a product
More from Magic
Why does my nappy bin smell?
Magic bin bag rolls
Frequently asked questions
Visit magicbabyproducts.com.au for the full Magic range, or shop at coolkidz.com.au .

articles.title: Magic Heka M telescopic nappy bin: size, capacity and colours
articles.text:
The Heka M is the medium size in the Magic Heka range. It has the same wide 28.5 cm body and drop and turn wave seal as the Heka L, in a shorter, smaller bin.
Size and capacity
Capacity: 30 litres
Width: 28.5 cm
Design: Telescopic, extends in height as needed
Mechanism: Drop and turn, patented wave seal
Material: 100% recycled, GRS traceable
Bags: Standard bin liner or Magic bag
The Heka M holds fewer nappies than the 40 litre Heka L. Nappy capacity always depends on nappy size, so expect fewer nappies per bag as your baby grows.
How it works
There are no refill cartridges and no film to thread. Drop the nappy into the opening and turn the top. The drum swings the nappy into the sealed part of the bin and the wave seal closes behind it, keeping odours locked in the chamber below. The drop and turn design can be used with one hand, so your other hand can stay with your baby.
Always bring the top back to its resting position after each change. When the bin needs more room, twist the base and the Heka M extends in height. It collapses again for storage, travel or the car.
Colours
The Heka M is sold in Australia in three colours.
Beige.
White.
Lichen.
Best for
Families who like the wide Heka body but want a shorter bin than the Heka L.
Homes that want a nappy bin that works with ordinary bin liners rather than cartridges.
Parents who want to keep using the bin after the nappy years: the Heka bathroom lid fits both the Heka M and Heka L and turns the base into an everyday household bin.
Good to know
Magic nappy bags work best for odour control, but the Heka M also takes standard bin liners. Avoid very thin supermarket bags, which may not seal properly.

articles.title: Magic Heka L telescopic nappy bin: size, capacity and colours
articles.text:
The Heka L is the flagship of the Magic range and the largest bin, with a 40 litre capacity for fewer bag changes. It is telescopic and wide bodied, and uses the same drop and turn wave seal as every Magic bin.
Size and capacity
Capacity: 40 litres
Nappies held: Up to 45 (approximate)
Dimensions: 28.5 cm wide x 63 cm high
Design: Telescopic, extends in height as needed
Mechanism: Drop and turn, patented wave seal
Material: 100% recycled, GRS traceable
In the box: Bin only
The nappy count is based on newborn and infant sizing. Expect fewer nappies per bag as your baby, and their nappies, grow.
How it works
Drop the nappy into the opening and turn the top. The drum swings the nappy into the sealed part of the bin and the wave seal closes behind it, so odours stay in the chamber below. There are no cartridges to load or film to thread, and the design can be used one handed.
Bring the top back to its resting position after every change. Twist the base to extend the bin as nappies build up, and collapse it again for storage, travel or the car.
Colours
The Heka L comes in seven colours, all with the same mechanism.
Beige.
Lichen.
White.
Blush Pink.
Concrete.
Pigeon Blue.
Graphite.
Best for
Busy households that want the biggest capacity in the range and fewer bag changes.
Rooms with space for the 28.5 cm Heka footprint, the widest in the range.
Parents who want a second life for the bin: add the Heka bathroom lid, sold in matching colours, and it becomes a regular bathroom or household bin.
Bags are not included
The Heka L ships as the bin only. It works with standard bin liners or Magic bin bags, which are made to fit the wave seal. Avoid very thin supermarket bags.

articles.title: Magic Thoth L slimline nappy bin: size, capacity and colours
articles.text:
The Thoth L is Magic's slimline bin. It is the same height and uses the same telescopic drop and turn mechanism as the Heka L, but with a narrower 24 cm footprint for tighter nurseries and bathrooms.
Size and capacity
Capacity: 28 litres
Nappies held: Up to 35 (approximate)
Dimensions: 24 cm wide x 63 cm high
Design: Slimline and telescopic
Mechanism: Drop and turn, patented wave seal
Material: 100% recycled, GRS traceable
In the box: Bin, 1 nappy bag roll and 1 dispenser
Nappy capacity depends on nappy size and is based on newborn and infant sizing, so you will fit fewer nappies per bag as your baby grows.
How it works
Drop the nappy into the opening and turn the top. The drum swings it into the sealed part of the bin and the wave seal closes behind it. Always bring the top back to its resting position after a change.
Because the Thoth L is telescopic, you can twist the base to extend it as the nappies pile up, then collapse it again for storage, travel or the car. It uses the same mechanism as the Heka bins, so the Heka and Thoth video guide covers it too.
Colours
The Thoth L comes in six colours.
Beige.
Lichen.
White.
Concrete.
Blush Pink.
Pigeon Blue.
Best for
Small bathrooms, nurseries and other spaces where floor space is tight.
Parents who want a starter kit, as the Thoth L comes with a bag roll and dispenser.
Families who want a second life for the bin: the Thoth bathroom lid fits the Thoth L and turns it into a regular household bin.
Use the right lid
The Thoth bathroom lid is made for the Thoth L. The Heka bathroom lid is a different accessory made for the Heka M and Heka L.

articles.title: Magic Majestic nappy bin: size, capacity and how it works
articles.text:
The Majestic is the entry point to the Magic range. It is a compact, fixed-height bin that uses the same drop and turn wave seal as the Heka and Thoth bins, in a smaller size.
Size and capacity
Capacity: 20 litres
Nappies held: Up to 25 (approximate)
Dimensions: 24 cm wide x 52 cm high
Design: Fixed height, not telescopic
Mechanism: Drop and turn, patented wave seal
Material: 100% recycled, GRS traceable
In the box: Bin, 1 nappy bag roll and 1 dispenser
The nappy count is based on newborn and infant sizing. Larger nappies take up more room, so expect fewer per bag as your baby grows.
How it works
The Majestic works a little differently from the telescopic bins. It sits open in the stand-by position, ready for the next nappy.
Drop the nappy straight through the opening. There is no bag threading and no touching the waste.
Turn the handle forward and back. The nappy moves into the sealed, odourless part of the bin.
Leave the bin in stand-by, with the cup open and not with the rounded side facing up, so no smell escapes.
Emptying the Majestic
Press the small side button to release the top.
Lift the top off together with the bag.
Twist the bag a few times to seal it, then tear it from the holder.
Fit a new bag. A standard bin liner or a Magic bin bag both work.
Colours and best for
The Majestic is sold in Lichen, Beige and White.
Parents who want a compact bin for a smaller space.
Anyone who prefers a fixed-height bin to a taller telescopic one.
Families who will not need a bathroom lid later, as there is no bathroom lid accessory for the Majestic.
Keep it in stand-by
Leaving the Majestic with the rounded side facing up breaks the seal path and is the easiest way to let odours out. Always return it to stand-by after a change.

articles.title: Choosing the right Magic nappy bin: Heka, Thoth or Majestic
articles.text:
Every Magic nappy bin uses the same patented drop and turn wave seal, works with standard bin liners and carries the same 1 year warranty. What changes between them is capacity, footprint, height and whether a bathroom lid is available.
The range side by side
Heka L: 40 litres, up to 45 nappies, 28.5 x 63 cm, telescopic
Heka M: 30 litres, 28.5 cm wide, shorter than the Heka L, telescopic
Thoth L: 28 litres, up to 35 nappies, 24 x 63 cm, telescopic
Majestic: 20 litres, up to 25 nappies, 24 x 52 cm, fixed height
Dimensions are width x height. Nappy counts are approximate and based on newborn and infant sizing, so expect fewer nappies per bag as your baby grows.
Which one suits your home
Choose the Heka L for the biggest capacity in the range and fewer bag changes, if you have room for the widest 28.5 cm footprint.
Choose the Heka M for the wide Heka body in a shorter, smaller bin.
Choose the Thoth L if you are tight on space: it is the same height as the Heka L with a slimline 24 cm footprint.
Choose the Majestic if a compact, fixed-height bin suits your space better than a taller telescopic one.
What comes in the box
Thoth L: bin, 1 nappy bag roll and 1 dispenser.
Majestic: bin, 1 nappy bag roll and 1 dispenser.
Heka L: bin only.
After the nappy years
The Heka and Thoth bins can have a second life. Add the matching bathroom lid and the base becomes a regular bathroom, laundry or bedroom bin. The Heka bathroom lid fits the Heka M and Heka L, and the Thoth bathroom lid fits the Thoth L. There is no bathroom lid for the Majestic.

articles.title: Magic nappy bags and bag rolls: which bags fit your bin
articles.text:
Magic bins have no refill cartridges and no proprietary bag system. Every Magic bin takes an ordinary plastic bag, and Magic also makes its own bin bags designed for the wave seal.
Which bags work
Most plastic bags and standard bin liners work in every Magic bin, and higher quality bags give the best results. Very thin supermarket shopping bags can stretch or fail to seal around the drum, so avoid them. Our guide Cleaning and odour tips for your Magic nappy bin covers how to check a bag before you fit it.
Magic bin bags
Magic bin bags are made to fit the wave seal for the best odour control. They are three layered, made from recycled plastic, and designed to help lock in odours for up to two weeks when used correctly.
Pack: Magic Bin Bag Roll, 3 pack
Bags per pack: 45
Fits: Heka M, Heka L, Thoth L and Majestic
Material: 100% recycled
Starter rolls and how long a pack lasts
The Thoth L and Majestic each come with one nappy bag roll and a dispenser in the box. The Heka L ships as the bin only, so you will need bags or a bag roll to get started.
How long a pack lasts depends on the size of your bin and how many nappies your baby goes through. Nappy capacity depends on nappy size, so bags fill faster as your baby grows.
Taking a full bag out
Press the small release button on the side and lift the top off with the bag. Twist the bag a few times to seal it. On a Heka or Thoth, tie the bag and lift it out. On a Majestic, tear it from the holder. Then fit a new bag.
Bag safety
Always keep plastic bags away from children, and store bag rolls in a locked or out of reach place.

articles.title: Magic nappy bin troubleshooting: lid, seal and release button
articles.text:
Most problems with a Magic nappy bin come down to how the top, the seal or the bag is being used. Work through the issue that matches yours below. For bag checks and cleaning steps, see our guide Cleaning and odour tips for your Magic nappy bin.
The top will not open when the bag is full
This is not a fault. The top is designed to stay locked until you release it.
Press the small release button on the side of the bin.
Carefully lift the top section off together with the bag.
Twist the bag a few times to seal it.
On a Heka or Thoth, tie the bag and lift it out. On a Majestic, tear it from the holder.
Fit a new bag and put the top back on until it clicks.
Odour escapes straight after a change
Turn the top all the way. A lid that is rested shut but not turned will not engage the wave seal, so odour escapes instead of staying in the chamber below.
On the Heka and Thoth, always bring the top back to its resting position after each change.
On the Majestic, turn the handle forward and back, then leave it in stand-by with the cup open, not with the rounded side facing up.
The bag splits or will not seal
Thin, flimsy bags can stretch or fail to seal properly around the drum. Switch to a better quality bin liner or a Magic bin bag, and check each bag for holes before fitting it. Make sure the top of the bag is tucked under the rim so the seal can close over it.
The bin fills faster than expected
Nappy counts are approximate and based on newborn and infant sizing, so the bin holds fewer nappies as your baby grows.
On a Heka or Thoth, twist the base to extend the bin and give it more room.
The Majestic is fixed height and does not extend.
Watch it done
The Magic video guides page shows each bin in real use, including how to use the Heka and Thoth telescopic bins, a Heka M tutorial covering loading, sealing and emptying, and the Majestic in action.
Still noticing a smell?
A full hand wash of the top and drum usually fixes a lingering smell. The steps are in our guide Cleaning and odour tips for your Magic nappy bin. Never put any part of the bin in the dishwasher.

articles.title: Magic nappy bin warranty: what is covered and how to claim
articles.text:
Every Magic nappy bin carries a 1 year warranty, backed by Coolkidz Australia, the exclusive authorised distributor of Magic in Australia. All Magic warranty claims and support in Australia are handled by our team.
What is covered
Your warranty applies when:
The product has been used under normal conditions, for its intended purpose only.
The product has been maintained as described in the user manual.
A valid, dated proof of purchase is provided. This applies to original and second-hand owners.
The product is in its original condition, with genuine Magic parts only.
What is not covered
Normal wear and tear, including changes in colour or surface finish.
Damage from sun exposure, heat, moisture, humidity or pollution.
Damage from accidents, impact, tipping, misuse or overloading.
Damage during transport, including as luggage.
Consequential or indirect loss, including injury or property damage.
Use of accessories or components not supplied or approved by Magic.
How to make a claim
Send us a request with your proof of purchase, a description of the issue, and photos or a video where relevant.
If your claim is approved, we will send you return instructions.
Once we receive the product, it is inspected against the warranty policy and Australian Consumer Law.
We then arrange a repair, replacement, refund or store credit.
Your rights under Australian Consumer Law
This warranty is in addition to your rights under Australian Consumer Law. Our goods come with guarantees that cannot be excluded. You are entitled to a replacement or refund for a major failure, and to compensation for any other reasonably foreseeable loss or damage.
Separate from the warranty, the Magic Australia returns policy allows 30 days from the date of receipt to return a product that is unopened and in its original condition.
Look after your bin
Hand wash only and never use a dishwasher. Keeping the bin out of strong sun and heat also protects your warranty, as damage from sun and heat is not covered.

articles.title: Using Mamave Bubba products on your baby
articles.text:
The Mamave Bubba range is made for babies and young children. This guide covers what each product is and how to use it.
What is in the Bubba range
Bubba's Wash: an all-in-one wash for hair and body, so you only need one product at bath time. Pump a small amount into the bath and cleanse your baby's skin with a soft washcloth, or lather it over their body and hair with a soft sponge or your hands.
Bubba's Moisturiser: a daily cream. It works best after a bath while the skin is still slightly damp, but you can also apply it to dry skin. Massage it in gently using circular motions.
Bubba's Massage Oil: a light plant oil for baby massage. Warm a small amount between your hands, then massage gently into the tummy, legs and arms. Add more as needed.
Bubba's Barrier Cream: a fragrance free cream for nappy change time. Apply a thick layer to your baby's bottom so it forms a barrier between the wet nappy and their skin.
Using the moisturiser and oil together
If your baby's skin looks extra dry, apply Bubba's Moisturiser first, then follow with Bubba's Massage Oil.
When to start
Mamave recommends waiting until your baby is at least one month old before using skincare products, because newborn skin is very delicate in the first month.
Scent
Bubba's Moisturiser and Bubba's Massage Oil are lightly scented with lavender and ylang ylang essential oils. Bubba's Wash contains mandarin essential oil. Bubba's Barrier Cream has no fragrance.
Patch test first
Mamave suggests patch testing before you use any skincare product. If irritation occurs, stop using the product and see your doctor. If your baby has a diagnosed skin condition, check with your doctor before use.
Need more help?
Send us a request and our Melbourne team will help.

articles.title: Using Mamave Mumma products in pregnancy and after birth
articles.text:
The Mamave Mumma range is designed for pregnancy and the months after birth. This guide covers what each product is and how to use it.
What is in the Mumma range
Mumma's Oil: a body oil. Warm a small amount between your hands, then massage it into your belly, thighs, hips and bottom in circular motions. You can apply it up to three times a day.
Mumma's Moisturiser: a daily body cream. Apply generously to your belly, thighs, hips and bottom and massage in circular motions until absorbed. You can use it up to three times a day.
Mumma's Scrub: an exfoliating body scrub. Take a small handful, massage it onto your body in gentle circular motions, then rinse with water.
Mumma's Soak: bath salts. Sprinkle a handful into your bath water and let it dissolve before you hop in.
Getting the most from the oil and moisturiser
Both are best applied after a shower or bath while your skin is still slightly damp. You can also apply them to dry skin. Mamave recommends using the two together for the best results. Apply Mumma's Moisturiser first, then follow with Mumma's Oil.
After birth
You can keep using the whole Mumma range after your baby arrives. The products are made for adult skin, so you can also use them when you are not pregnant.
About stretch marks
Mamave is clear that nothing can completely prevent stretch marks, and it does not guarantee that its products will.
Scent
The Mumma range is lightly scented with lavender and frankincense essential oils.
Check if you are unsure
Mamave suggests patch testing first. For Mumma's Soak, ask your doctor about safe bath temperature and how long to bathe during pregnancy. If you are unsure about using any product while pregnant, check with your doctor or midwife. If irritation occurs, stop using the product and see your doctor.
Need more help?
Send us a request and our Melbourne team will help.
