articles.title: Mamave Bubba's Wash: how to use it at bath time
articles.text:
Bubba's Wash is a gentle all-in-one wash for your baby's hair and body, so one bottle covers the whole bath. Here is how to use it and what is inside.
Two ways to use it
Mamave gives two ways to use Bubba's Wash. Choose whichever suits your bath routine.
Pump a small amount of the wash into the bath water.
Gently cleanse your baby's skin using a soft washcloth.
Or, if you prefer to wash directly:
Pump a small amount onto a soft sponge or into your hands.
Gently lather it over your baby's body and hair.
What is in the formula
Bubba's Wash uses naturally derived, coconut-based surfactants for mild cleansing and is pH balanced for baby skin. Its key ingredients are:
Panthenol (pro-vitamin B5), which helps hydrate and support the skin barrier.
Borage seed oil, which is naturally rich in GLA (Gamma Linolenic Acid).
Calendula flower extract, traditionally used to calm and comfort the skin.
Aloe vera, known for its soothing and cooling properties.
Pomegranate extract for antioxidant support.
Naturally derived mandarin essential oil, which scents the wash, and cucumber seed oil.
The wash does not contain parabens or the sulphates SLS and SLES. It does contain sodium coco sulphate, which Mamave describes as a mild, gentle surfactant derived from coconuts. Bubba's Wash is vegan and cruelty free.
Size and details
Size: 250mL pump bottle
Use for: Hair and body, every bath
Scent: Naturally derived mandarin essential oil
Made in: Australia
After the bath
Mamave suggests avoiding soap bars on babies, because soap is basic (above pH 9) and can disrupt the skin's natural acid mantle. After the bath you can follow up with Bubba's Moisturiser or Bubba's Massage Oil, ideally while your baby's skin is still slightly damp.
Good to know
As with any skincare, Mamave recommends a patch test first. If your baby has a diagnosed skin condition, check with your GP or pharmacist before use.

articles.title: Mamave Bubba's Moisturiser: when and how to apply it
articles.text:
Bubba's Moisturiser is Mamave's daily cream for baby skin, made to hydrate and calm dry skin after the bath. This guide covers when to apply it and what is in it.
How to apply it
Apply after the bath, while your baby's skin is still slightly damp. Skin absorbs creams better when slightly damp, which helps lock in extra moisture.
Take a small amount of moisturiser.
Massage it gently into your baby's skin in circular motions.
Repeat daily, or as part of your after bath routine.
You can also apply it to dry skin at other times of the day.
Using it with Bubba's Massage Oil
If your baby's skin is looking extra dry, Mamave suggests applying Bubba's Moisturiser first and then following with Bubba's Massage Oil for extra hydration. Mamave also describes the moisturiser as formulated to assist with baby massage.
Key ingredients
Squalane, a lightweight hydrator that mimics the skin's natural oils to help lock in moisture.
Borage seed oil, naturally rich in Gamma Linolenic Acid (GLA) to help relieve dryness and support the skin barrier.
Mango seed butter, rich and conditioning to help soften skin.
MCT oil for lightweight, silky hydration.
Calendula flower extract, traditionally used to calm and comfort the skin.
Pomegranate extract for antioxidant support.
Lavender and ylang ylang essential oils for a light, calming scent. There is no artificial fragrance.
Bubba's Moisturiser is vegan and cruelty free.
Sizes
Full size: 250mL pump bottle
Travel mini: 30mL
When to use: Daily, after the bath
Scent: Lavender and ylang ylang essential oils
When to start
Mamave recommends waiting until your baby is at least one month old before using skincare products, because newborn skin is very delicate while its natural barrier forms. Patch test first, and check with your GP or pharmacist if your baby has a diagnosed skin condition.

articles.title: Mamave Bubba's Massage Oil: baby massage step by step
articles.text:
Bubba's Massage Oil is a light blend of plant oils made for daily baby massage. Here is how Mamave suggests using it, and what is in the bottle.
Baby massage, step by step
Choose a time after the bath, while your baby's skin is still slightly damp. Skin absorbs oils better when slightly damp. You can also use the oil on dry skin.
Put a small amount of oil into your hands.
Rub your hands together to warm the oil.
Massage gently into your baby's skin in circular motions, paying careful attention to the tummy, legs and arms.
Apply more oil as required.
If your baby's skin is extra dry, apply Bubba's Moisturiser first and follow with the Massage Oil. Mamave describes daily massage as a calming ritual for both baby and parent.
Cradle cap
Mamave says Bubba's Massage Oil can also be used to gently support cradle cap care. Warm a small amount in your hands and massage it in gently. For any questions about your baby's scalp or skin, talk to your GP or pharmacist.
What is in the oil
The blend includes safflower, apricot kernel, grape seed, sunflower, jojoba (certified organic), borage seed, rosehip, olive and evening primrose oils with natural vitamin E, aloe vera and calendula extract. The golden ingredients are:
Borage seed oil, naturally rich in GLA to nourish and protect delicate skin.
Rosehip oil, rich in skin loving vitamins.
Evening primrose oil, high in essential fatty acids to help soothe dryness.
Aloe vera and calendula extract, traditionally used to calm the skin.
It is lightly scented with lavender and ylang ylang essential oils, with no artificial fragrance. It is vegan and cruelty free. The oil contains apricot kernel oil, so check the full ingredient list if your family has any sensitivities.
Sizes
Full size: 100mL bottle
Travel mini: 30mL
When to use: Daily massage
Scent: Lavender and ylang ylang essential oils
When to start
Mamave recommends waiting until your baby is at least one month old before using skincare products, while their natural skin barrier forms. Patch test first, and check with your GP or pharmacist if your baby has a diagnosed skin condition.

articles.title: Mamave Bubba's Barrier Cream: using it at nappy change
articles.text:
Bubba's Barrier Cream is Mamave's fragrance free zinc oxide cream for the nappy area. It forms a breathable layer between a wet nappy and your baby's skin.
Nappy change routine
Remove the wet or dirty nappy and clean your baby's bottom as usual.
Let the skin dry.
Apply a thick layer of Bubba's Barrier Cream to your baby's bum or other rash affected areas.
Put on a fresh nappy. The cream creates a barrier between the wet nappy and delicate skin, helping protect it from moisture and irritation caused by constant rubbing.
Repeat at each nappy change, as needed.
Other uses
Mamave says you can also apply Bubba's Barrier Cream to:
Small cuts and abrasions on your baby's skin.
Dribble rash.
Skin chafe, such as in arm, leg, neck and tummy rolls.
If a rash or skin problem is not settling, looks infected or worries you, talk to your GP or pharmacist.
What is in it
The cream is fragrance free, because it is applied to delicate areas prone to rashes. It is vegan and cruelty free. Its golden ingredients are:
Zinc oxide, which creates a gentle, breathable barrier against moisture and irritation.
Castor seed oil, traditionally used to protect and comfort irritated skin.
Rice bran wax, a plant wax (and vegan alternative to beeswax) that helps seal in moisture.
Mango seed butter and MCT oil for softness and hydration.
Aloe vera and calendula extract to help calm the skin.
Pomegranate extract for antioxidant support.
The formula also contains apricot kernel oil, olive oil, borage seed oil and sunflower oil.
Size and details
Size: 100mL tube
Scent: Fragrance free
When to use: Each nappy change, as needed
Made in: Australia
Before you start
Patch test first, as with any skincare. If your baby has a diagnosed skin condition, or a rash that is not improving, check with your GP or pharmacist.

articles.title: Mamave Mumma's Oil and Mumma's Moisturiser: how to use them together
articles.text:
Mumma's Oil and Mumma's Moisturiser are made to be used together on changing skin during pregnancy and after birth. This guide covers how to apply each one and what makes them different.
Which does what
Mumma's Oil is a concentrated massage oil that supports skin elasticity, made for massaging into the bump, hips and thighs.
Mumma's Moisturiser is a daily cream for everyday hydration, with vitamin C rich pomegranate and cranberry extracts.
Mamave recommends using both together for the best results, Mumma's Moisturiser first and then Mumma's Oil.
How to apply
Apply after a shower or bath while your skin is still slightly damp, as skin absorbs oils and creams better and locks in extra moisture. You can also apply to dry skin.
Start with Mumma's Moisturiser. Apply it generously to your belly, thighs, hips and bottom, massaging in circular motions until fully absorbed.
Follow with Mumma's Oil. Put a small amount in your hands and rub them together to warm it.
Massage the oil gently into the same areas in circular motions, applying generously.
Use each up to three times a day for best results.
Key ingredients
Mumma's Oil is a blend of safflower, sunflower, grape seed, camellia, jojoba, argan and evening primrose oils with natural vitamin E. The jojoba and argan are certified organic.
Mumma's Moisturiser includes mango seed butter, squalane, MCT oil, argan oil, aloe vera, pomegranate and cranberry extracts, and a plant derived vegan alternative to lanolin.
Both are lightly scented with lavender and frankincense essential oils, with no artificial fragrance.
Sizes and when to start
Mumma's Oil: 100mL bottle, travel mini 30mL
Mumma's Moisturiser: 250mL pump bottle, travel mini 30mL
How often: Up to 3 times a day
Scent: Lavender and frankincense essential oils
Mamave suggests starting as soon as you find out you are pregnant, and continuing postpartum. Both are formulated for adult skin, so you can keep using them when you are not pregnant.
About stretch marks
Mamave is clear that nothing can completely prevent stretch marks and it cannot guarantee prevention. Patch test first, and if you have questions about skincare in pregnancy, ask your GP, midwife or pharmacist.

articles.title: Mamave Mumma's Scrub and Mumma's Soak: shower and bath routine
articles.text:
Mumma's Scrub and Mumma's Soak complete the Mumma range: a body scrub for the shower and bath salts for a relaxing soak.
Using Mumma's Scrub
Take a small handful of scrub and rub it between your hands.
Massage it onto your body, focusing on your belly, thighs, hips and bottom.
Rub in gentle circular motions.
Rinse off with water.
Use it in the shower as needed to buff away dry, dull skin. The scrub is made with sucrose (natural sugar), soya bean oil, silica, evening primrose, argan, safflower and sunflower oils, vitamin E, glycerin and cranberry extract, lightly scented with lavender and frankincense essential oils. It contains soya bean oil, so check the full ingredient list if you have sensitivities.
Using Mumma's Soak
Run your bath.
Sprinkle a handful of salts into the bath water.
Let the salts dissolve.
Hop in and relax.
The soak contains salt, magnesium sulphate (Epsom salt), glycerin, cranberry extract and chamomile extract, lightly scented with lavender and frankincense essential oils. Mamave describes magnesium sulphate as supporting deep muscle relaxation, and chamomile as traditionally used to ease tired, aching muscles.
Sizes and details
Mumma's Scrub: 250g pouch
Mumma's Soak: 250g pouch
Scrub, how often: In the shower, as needed
Soak, how often: Bath time, as needed
Storage: Store in a cool, dry place
Who can use them
Both are designed for pregnancy and postpartum, and Mamave recommends continuing after your baby arrives. Mamave says the scrub can be used by anyone, and the soak can be used if you are not pregnant. Mamave even suggests your partner may like to sneak some.
Bathing in pregnancy
Mamave asks you to check with your doctor about safe bath water temperature and how long to bathe during pregnancy before using Mumma's Soak. Your GP or midwife can advise. Patch test the scrub first, as with any skincare.

articles.title: Mamave travel minis and Collection Travel Bag: sizes and what to pack
articles.text:
Mamave makes four of its favourites in 30mL travel minis, plus a zip up travel bag to carry them. They suit hospital bags and weekends away, or trying a product before you buy the full size.
The four travel minis
Each mini is a 30mL size of the full size product.
Mumma's Oil Travel Mini: 30mL (full size 100mL)
Mumma's Moisturiser Travel Mini: 30mL (full size 250mL)
Bubba's Massage Oil Travel Mini: 30mL (full size 100mL)
Bubba's Moisturiser Travel Mini: 30mL (full size 250mL)
Bubba's Wash, Bubba's Barrier Cream, Mumma's Scrub and Mumma's Soak are not currently listed as minis.
Good uses for the minis
Packing a hospital bag for the birth.
Weekends away and travel.
Trying a formula before you buy the full size.
The minis are used the same way as the full sizes. For example, warm a small amount of Mumma's Oil or Bubba's Massage Oil between your hands before massaging it in, and apply the moisturisers to slightly damp skin after a bath or shower.
Mamave Collection Travel Bag
The Collection Travel Bag is a toiletry bag sized for your Mamave skincare, baby products or the nappy change bag. It keeps all your essentials in one place and comes in Mamave's signature Warm Grey colourway.
Closure: Easy zip up
Inside: Single compartment
Colour: Warm Grey with white zip and round pull
Material: Durable nylon

articles.title: Mamave ingredients explained: what is in the range and what is left out
articles.text:
Mamave formulas are developed by a cosmetic chemist and made in small batches in Australia. Here is what goes in, what stays out, and how to check a product suits your skin.
What Mamave leaves out
No retinoids.
No parabens.
No artificial or synthetic fragrance.
No synthetic colours.
No petrochemicals or mineral oils.
No almond or peanut oils.
SLS and SLES free.
Vegan and cruelty free.
Mamave's preservative system is benzyl alcohol and dehydroacetic acid, which it describes as free from parabens, isothiazolinones and formaldehyde.
Key ingredients you will see
GLA (Gamma Linolenic Acid): a fatty acid found in plant oils such as borage seed and evening primrose, used across the range to help support the skin barrier and relieve dryness.
Squalane: a lightweight emollient similar to the skin's natural oils, in both moisturisers.
Zinc oxide: forms a protective barrier on the skin, in Bubba's Barrier Cream.
Bis-Diglyceryl Polyacyladipate-2: a plant derived alternative to lanolin.
Rice bran wax: a vegan alternative to beeswax.
Sodium coco sulphate: a mild, coconut derived cleanser in Bubba's Wash.
Mamave's Ingredients Glossary explains every ingredient in its formulas from A to Z.
How each product is scented
Mumma's Oil, Moisturiser, Scrub, Soak: Lavender and frankincense essential oils
Bubba's Moisturiser and Massage Oil: Lavender and ylang ylang essential oils
Bubba's Wash: Naturally derived mandarin essential oil
Bubba's Barrier Cream: Fragrance free
Allergies and patch testing
The range is free from almond and peanut oils, but some products contain other plant oils. For example, Bubba's Massage Oil and Bubba's Barrier Cream contain apricot kernel oil, and Mumma's Scrub contains soya bean oil. Full ingredient lists are on each product page.
As with any skincare, Mamave recommends a patch test first. If you or your baby have a diagnosed skin condition, or you are unsure about using a product in pregnancy, check with your GP, midwife or pharmacist.

articles.title: Using the ride-on seat on your MiaMily luggage
articles.text:
Your MiaMily suitcase has a built-in seat, so your child can ride while you pull. This guide covers who can ride and how to set the seat up safely.
Who can ride
MiaMily does not set a minimum age. Your child must be able to sit up without help.
The seat is rated to 100 kg in total , and that figure includes whatever is packed in the case. Older children and adults can sit on it too.
The Carry On, Check In, Carry On Plus and Check In Plus have a child safety belt. The Carry On Pro has a shell you can sit on but no child belt, so it suits older children, teens and adults.
Setting up the seat
Stop the case on a flat surface. On the Plus range, press the wheel brake first.
Lift the seat up from the shell until it locks upright.
Sit your child facing forward and fasten the safety belt snugly.
Hang your nappy bag or tote on the hook on the seat back, then raise the handle to a height that suits you.
On the Plus range, release the brake, then pull smoothly and stay beside your child.
Safety rules
Always use the belt and always supervise your child.
Use the seat on flat surfaces only.
Never use it on escalators, stairs, travelators or slopes.
Do not use the seat as a step.
When nobody is riding
The seat makes a handy shelf for a nappy bag, tote or briefcase. When you are finished, fold it flat against the shell.

articles.title: Setting the lock and caring for your MiaMily luggage
articles.text:
A few simple habits will keep your MiaMily luggage working well trip after trip. Here is how to set the combination lock, clean the case and get ready to fly.
Setting the lock code
Your case arrives with the code set to 000 . To choose your own:
Open the lock and find the small pin inside the lock housing.
Move the pin from A to B.
Dial your new three-digit code.
Move the pin back to A, then test the lock once before you pack.
The lock is TSA-approved and has no key. If your bag is chosen for inspection, security staff can open it with a universal key. Keep a note of your code somewhere other than the luggage tag.
Cleaning and storage
Wipe the hard shell with a soft, damp cloth and mild soap.
Avoid solvents and abrasive cleaners or pads, as they can dull the textured finish.
After a trip, check the wheels for hair and grit. A wheel that drags usually has something wrapped around it.
Let the lining air dry completely before you pack or store the case.
Store it with the seat folded flat and the handle down.
Before you fly
The Carry On measures 51 x 38 x 29 cm including wheels and weighs 4.3 kg empty. The Carry On Plus measures 51 x 39 x 30 cm and weighs 4.8 kg. Cabin size and weight limits differ between airlines, so check with your airline before you travel. The Check In and Check In Plus are checked luggage.
Warranty
MiaMily luggage bought in Australia from an authorised retailer comes with a Limited Lifetime Warranty for manufacturing defects in materials and workmanship. Normal wear and tear, cosmetic marks, misuse and airline handling damage are not covered. Keep your proof of purchase.

articles.title: MiaMily Carry On: features, packing and flying with it
articles.text:
The Carry On is the original MiaMily ride-on: a cabin-size hard-shell suitcase with the patented built-in seat, a child seatbelt and a bag hook. Here is what your case includes and how to get the most from it.
What your Carry On includes
A patented built-in seat for children and adults, rated to 100 kg in total including what is packed inside.
A child seatbelt, included.
A bag hook on the seat back for a nappy bag or tote.
Four 360° spinner wheels.
A telescopic handle with four heights.
A universal TSA combination lock with no key to lose.
An anti-scratch textured polycarbonate shell, designed to hide the scuffs of real travel.
Specifications
Dimensions: 51 × 38 × 29 cm, wheels included
Capacity: 43 litres
Weight: 4.3 kg empty
Opening: Clamshell, two halves, five interior compartments
Lock: Universal TSA combination lock
Wheel brake: No
Shell: Polycarbonate
Seat: Polypropylene
Lining: Polyester
Packing the clamshell
The Carry On opens in the centre into two halves, with five interior compartments so everything has a place. Because it is a clamshell, it opens out across the floor. If you would rather pack from the top into one deep space, that is how the Carry On Plus differs.
The Carry On has no front pocket, so keep the things you need in a queue, such as snacks, wipes and passports, in a backpack slid over the handle rather than inside the case.
Taking it on the plane
MiaMily designs the Carry On to fit most airline overhead compartments. Cabin allowances differ between Australian domestic carriers and international airlines, some are tighter than the international norm, and the weight limit is often the stricter rule. A packed 43 litres adds up, so check your carrier's size and weight limits before you fly.
The Carry On suits trips from a weekend to about a week, with one child riding and the case staying with you from door to gate. For longer trips, bulky packing or more than one child, the 77 litre Check In is the bigger option.
No wheel brake on this model
The original Carry On does not have a wheel brake. Only load your child on a flat surface, always fasten the belt and stay beside them. Never use the seat on escalators, stairs, travelators or slopes.

articles.title: MiaMily Carry On Plus: top opening, pockets and wheel brake
articles.text:
The Carry On Plus keeps the patented built-in seat and child safety belt of the original Carry On, then changes how you pack and adds a wheel brake. This guide covers the features that are new on the Plus.
What is different on the Plus
Top-opening shell: the lid lifts vertically to reveal one deep, uninterrupted packing space instead of two halves.
Front pocket: reach snacks, toys, a tablet or passports without lifting your child off the seat.
Larger waterproof pocket to keep messes contained.
Thermal pocket to keep bottles and snacks cool.
Wheel brake that keeps the case still while your child is seated.
Integrated bag hook so your nappy bag stays attached and your hands stay free.
Telescopic handle with four height settings.
TSA-approved zip lock and an anti-scratch textured shell.
Specifications
Dimensions: 51 × 39 × 30 cm, wheels included
Capacity: 43 litres, the same as the original Carry On
Weight: 4.8 kg empty
Opening: Top-opening, one deep packing space, plus a quick-access front pocket
Lock: TSA-approved zip lock
Wheel brake: Yes
Seat: Built-in, 100 kg total capacity, child seatbelt included
Colours: Navy Blue and Burgundy Red
Using the wheel brake
Press the wheel brake whenever the case is parked: before your child climbs on, while they sit at a café table, and when you stop to unload at security. Release the brake before you start pulling again.
With the brake on, the built-in seat can double as a high chair on the go. Always belt your child in and stay with them.
Packing tips
Pack the main space from the top. Because the lid opens vertically, the case takes a strip of floor rather than the whole hotel room.
Keep your reach-first items in the front pocket: snacks, a drink, wipes, a small toy, the tablet and passports.
Put a bottle in the thermal pocket and anything that might leak in the waterproof pocket.
Brake on, belt on
Put the brake on before loading your child, fasten the belt every time and supervise them at all times. Use the seat on flat surfaces only, never on escalators, stairs, travelators or slopes.

articles.title: MiaMily Check In: size, packing and when to use it
articles.text:
The Check In brings the MiaMily ride-on to full suitcase size: 77 litres, the same patented seat and seatbelt, and a wider base for stability. Here is what it holds and how families use it.
Specifications
Dimensions: 66 × 45 × 31 cm, wheels included
Capacity: 77 litres
Weight: 6.5 kg empty
Opening: Clamshell, two halves
Lock: Universal TSA combination lock
Seat: Built-in, 100 kg total capacity including contents
Child seatbelt: Included
Wheel brake: No
Materials: Polycarbonate shell, polypropylene seat, polyester lining
What it includes
The patented built-in seat, for children and adults.
A child seatbelt and a bag hook on the seat back.
A wider base for stability at check-in size.
A telescopic handle with adjustable heights and four 360° spinner wheels.
An anti-scratch textured polycarbonate shell.
A Limited Lifetime Warranty.
How it compares with the Carry On
The Check In holds about 1.8 times as much as the Carry On. Empty, it weighs 2.2 kg more, which you will notice lifting it into the car boot but not while pulling it.
It is checked luggage, not a cabin case. The seat still earns its place: use it from the kerb to bag drop, and again from the baggage carousel to the car.
When the Check In makes sense
Overseas trips or holidays of a week or more.
Packing bulky items.
Packing for more than one child in one case.
A bigger child riding, where the wider base adds stability.
You already have a cabin bag and want the ride-on to be your checked case.
Seat safety
The 100 kg limit includes everything packed in the case, which matters more on a full 77 litre suitcase. Your child must be able to sit unassisted, always belted in and supervised, and the seat is for flat surfaces only, never escalators, stairs or travelators.

articles.title: MiaMily Check In Plus: top-opening packing and wheel brakes
articles.text:
The Check In Plus is the full-size member of the Plus range. It keeps the built-in seat and child safety belt, opens from the top into one deep space and adds wheel brakes.
Specifications
Dimensions: 65.5 × 46 × 33 cm, wheels included
Capacity: 77 litres
Weight: 5.9 kg empty
Opening: Top-opening, one deep packing space, plus a front pocket
Lock: TSA-approved zip lock
Seat: Built-in, 100 kg total capacity including contents
Child seatbelt: Included
Wheel brake: Yes
Colours: Navy Blue and Burgundy Red
It holds the same 77 litres as the original Check In and, at 5.9 kg, weighs less than the original's 6.5 kg.
Packing from the top
Most suitcases split into two halves. The Check In Plus opens vertically to give one deep, uninterrupted packing space, so it takes up less floor space in a tight hotel room and fits bulky items such as shoes, boots and jackets.
Use the large waterproof pocket for liquids.
Keep things you need at the gate in the front pocket, so you do not have to open the main case.
Hang a nappy bag or tote on the bag hook to keep your hands free.
Wheel brakes and the seat
The wheel brakes add security while someone is seated. Put them on before your child climbs on and release them before you pull. The telescopic handle has four height settings.
Once you land, the built-in seat is also a stable spot to stack extra bags on the way to your accommodation, which is handy on multi-stop trips between hotels and apartments.
Safety rules
The 100 kg limit includes everything packed inside. Your child must sit unassisted, always be belted in and be supervised. Flat surfaces only, never escalators, stairs, travelators or slopes.

articles.title: MiaMily Carry On Pro: front opening, Sit Ready shell and who it suits
articles.text:
The Carry On Pro is the lightest and slimmest MiaMily cabin case. It opens from the front, has a zipperless TSA-approved lock and a reinforced shell you can sit on, but it is not a toddler ride-on.
Who it is for
The reinforced Sit Ready shell supports up to 100 kg, so it doubles as a seat during long waits, such as at the gate. The Carry On Pro does not have the child seatbelt or the seat-back bag hook of the Carry On, Check In and Plus models, so it suits older children, teens and adults rather than toddlers.
Specifications
Dimensions: 51 × 39 × 23 cm, wheels included
Capacity: 48 litres
Weight: 3.5 kg empty
Opening: Front-opening, top-down packing, quick-access compartment
Lock: Zipperless TSA-approved lock
Seat capacity: 100 kg
Child seatbelt: Not on this model
Wheel brake: No
Materials: Durable hard-shell plastic, fabric-lined interior
Colours: Black and Olive
Packing and quick access
The front-opening design lets you pack from the top down and grab essentials from the front without opening the whole case.
Use the quick-access compartment for snacks, toys, tablets, chargers and passports.
It has smooth 360° spinner wheels and an adjustable telescopic handle.
MiaMily designs it to fit most airline overhead bins. Check your airline's size and weight limits before you fly.
The zipperless lock
The Carry On Pro closes with a secure latch and an integrated TSA-approved lock rather than a zip. If your bag is chosen for inspection, security staff open it with a universal key instead of cutting the lock.
Not a ride-on for young children
The Carry On Pro has no child seatbelt. Use it as a seat for older children, teens and adults on flat ground only, and never as a step.

articles.title: MiaMily Expandable Backpack: pockets, expanding and the trolley sleeve
articles.text:
The MiaMily Expandable Backpack is the parent bag of the range. It grows from 15 to 30 litres when you need it and slides over the handle of your MiaMily suitcase.
Specifications
Dimensions: 44 × 31 × 11 cm
Depth expanded: 22 cm
Capacity: 15 litres, or 30 litres expanded
Pockets: 11 organisational pockets
Material: 100% recycled polyester, water-resistant
Zips: YKK
Colours: Slate Blue, Forest Green and Midnight Black
Expanding the backpack
An external expandable pocket on the front doubles the capacity, taking the backpack from 15 to 30 litres and from 11 cm to 22 cm deep. Keep it slim for work or a day out, and expand it when you need the extra room.
MiaMily designed it to be sleek enough for work and big enough for a weekend trip, so it is useful well beyond the airport. It is made from water-resistant, 100% recycled polyester with YKK zips.
Where everything goes
Laptop pocket.
Thermal water bottle pocket.
Anti-theft passport pocket.
Sunglasses pocket.
Umbrella pocket.
Magazine pocket.
Padded, adjustable shoulder straps.
Using it with your suitcase
A trolley sleeve on the back slides over the handle of any MiaMily suitcase, so the backpack rides on the case instead of on your shoulders. On travel days with the original Carry On, which has no front pocket, use the outside pocket of the backpack for the things you need in a queue: snacks, wipes, a small toy and passports.
The backpack does not have a seat. It is covered by MiaMily's Limited Lifetime Warranty.

articles.title: Flying with a toddler using MiaMily luggage: a gate-to-gate plan
articles.text:
Toddlers rarely mind the flight; it is the waiting, the carrying and the standing still they find hard. A travel day has several waits before the plane moves, and your MiaMily case can turn each one into a sit.
Before you leave home
Pack a reach-first pocket with snacks, a drink, wipes, a small toy, the tablet and passports.
On the Carry On Plus, use the front pocket and put the bottle in the thermal pocket.
On the original Carry On, use the outside pocket of a backpack slid over the handle.
Check your airline's cabin size and weight limits. Australian domestic limits can be tighter than international ones, and a packed 43 litre case adds up.
Arrive with time to spare.
Through the airport
At check-in and bag drop, belt your child onto the seat, hang your bag on the hook and let the queue move you.
At security, park the case (brake on if you have a Plus) and lift your child off before the conveyor. The case goes through the scanner and your child walks through with you. A three-digit TSA lock means there is no key to find.
At the gate, seats fill early. The MiaMily seat holds 100 kg, so when your child is tired of sitting, you can sit. Give your child a job, such as counting planes, holding the boarding passes or watching for the gate number.
At boarding, fold the seat flat and the case is a cabin case again.
On arrival, put the seat up again for the long walk to the taxi.
At the hotel
A top-opening Plus case opens vertically, so it takes a strip of floor rather than the whole room. If you are moving between hotels and apartments, the seat on the Check In Plus is also a stable place to stack extra bags.
Airport safety
Never ride on escalators, stairs, travelators or slopes, and take your child off before you reach one. Your child must sit unassisted, be belted in and be supervised at all times. The Carry On Pro has no child seatbelt and is not a ride-on for toddlers.

articles.title: MiaMily Limited Lifetime Warranty: what is covered and how to claim
articles.text:
MiaMily luggage bought in Australia from an authorised retailer comes with a Limited Lifetime Warranty. Coolkidz, the Australian distributor, handles every claim locally.
What is covered
The warranty covers manufacturing defects in materials and workmanship for the product's usable life, starting from the original date of purchase. It applies to:
Zippers that break or malfunction.
Handles that are broken or defective.
Wheels that are broken or defective.
Stitching defects that cause loose threads or open seams.
Defects in fabrics and materials, such as tears or fraying during normal use.
What is not covered
Normal wear and tear, such as scuffs, scratches or damage from regular use over time.
Misuse or abuse, including improper handling, accidents, excessive force, extreme conditions or improper care.
Cosmetic damage, such as scratches, dents or colour changes that do not affect how the case works.
Unauthorised repairs or alterations.
Damage caused by airline handling.
How to make a claim
Find your proof of purchase from an authorised MiaMily retailer in Australia.
Take clear photos of the defect.
Send us a request with details of the fault and your photos.
Our team checks whether the defect is covered.
If it is, we will, at our discretion, repair the product at no cost, replace it with the same or a comparable model, or offer a refund or store credit if repair or replacement is not possible.
You cover the cost of sending the product to us for evaluation. If the defect is covered, we cover the cost of sending the repaired or replacement product back to you.
Good to know
The warranty is non-transferable and applies only to the original purchaser.
It sits alongside, and does not limit, your rights under the Australian Consumer Law.
Only luggage bought from an authorised retailer is covered, so keep your receipt.

articles.title: Setting up your Nanit Pro camera
articles.text:
Every Nanit Pro system uses the same camera. What changes is the stand or mount that holds it above your baby's sleep space. This guide covers what you should find in the box and how each option goes together.
What is in the box
Nanit Pro camera.
Your stand or mount.
A newborn Breathing Band and newborn pyjamas.
USB-C cable and Australian power adapter.
Quick start guide.
The Floor Stand and Wall Mount systems also include a Flex Stand for travel. The Wall Mount system includes wall anchors.
Setting up each stand
Floor Stand: freestanding, with no drilling. Adjust the height so the camera sits directly over the cot. Allow about 10 minutes.
Wall Mount: fixes to the wall above the cot and has a channel for the cable. You will need a drill and the two wall anchors. Allow about 15 minutes.
Flex Stand: no tools needed. The flexible neck wraps onto a bassinet rail, shelf or travel cot, and it folds flat into its pouch. Allow about 5 minutes. Breathing motion monitoring does not work on the Flex Stand, because it needs the camera directly above the cot on a Floor Stand or Wall Mount.
Connecting to Wi-Fi
The camera needs a 2.4GHz home network. It will not connect to a network that is 5GHz only. If it will not connect:
Check that your network is 2.4GHz.
Move the camera within range of your router while you set it up.
Restart both the camera and the router, then try again.
Changing your setup later
Stands and mounts are sold separately, so you can add a different one later and keep using the same camera.
Need more help?
If something is missing from the box or the camera still will not connect, send us a request and our Melbourne team will help.
Get help with a product
More from Nanit
What's in the box
Find your setup
Frequently asked questions
Visit nanit.com.au for the full Nanit range, or shop at coolkidz.com.au .

articles.title: Nanit subscription, Wi-Fi and warranty questions
articles.text:
Here are answers to the questions Nanit owners ask most often once the camera is up and running.
Do you need a subscription?
No. Live HD video, two-way audio and instant alerts work without a plan. Nanit Insights is the optional plan that adds sleep analytics, extended video history and personalised guidance. It is included free with every camera for the first 3 months. When that ends, the core features keep working, and you can choose whether to continue Insights on a paid plan.
What Wi-Fi does the camera need?
The camera needs a 2.4GHz home Wi-Fi network. It will not connect to a network that is 5GHz only.
What happens if the internet drops?
The camera keeps working on your local network, so you can still see and hear your baby at home. Remote viewing and alerts return once it reconnects.
How does breathing motion monitoring work?
The camera reads the printed pattern on Nanit Breathing Wear, so no sensors touch your baby. You need at least one piece of Breathing Wear, and larger sizes are sold separately as your baby grows. Breathing motion monitoring needs the camera directly above the cot on a Floor Stand or Wall Mount, and does not work on the Flex Stand. Nanit is not a medical device and is not intended to diagnose, treat, monitor or prevent any medical condition, including SIDS. Always follow recommended safe sleep practices.
Can other carers use the app?
Yes. You can invite a partner, grandparent or nanny to your Parenting Team so they can view the camera too.
Can the camera play sounds?
Yes. Nanit Pro has four built-in sounds: birds, white noise, wind and waves. In the app you can set a timer for 30 or 60 minutes, or leave the sound playing continuously.
What warranty applies?
Nanit products bought from an authorised Australian retailer have a 1-year limited warranty from the date of delivery. It does not cover misuse, accidental damage, unauthorised repair, damage from incorrect installation or mounting, or problems caused by your home Wi-Fi or internet connection. Your rights under the Australian Consumer Law also apply.
Need more help?
Send us a request, and have your order number and a description of the fault ready.
Get help with a product

articles.title: Nanit Breathing Wear: Band and pyjama sizes, fit and care
articles.text:
Nanit Breathing Wear is what lets your Nanit camera track breathing motion. It is soft fabric printed with a pattern the camera reads from above the cot, with no sensors, wires or batteries.
How the pattern works
The camera sits above the cot and uses computer vision to follow the printed pattern on the Breathing Wear as your baby's chest rises and falls. The app shows this as breathing motion in real time, and sends an alert to your phone if breathing motion stops beyond Nanit's alert threshold.
There is nothing electronic in the Band or pyjamas, so the only thing touching your baby is fabric.
Your baby only needs to wear the pattern once, either as a Band or as pyjamas, not both.
Breathing motion monitoring needs a Nanit camera on a Wall Mount or Floor Stand, plus the Nanit app.
It does not work with the Flex Stand, because the camera needs to be directly above the cot.
Choosing a size
The Breathing Wear Band comes in three sizes and the Breathing Wear Pyjamas come in two. Most families size up every few months as their baby grows.
Band Small: Newborn to 3 months
Band Medium: 3 to 6 months
Band Large: 6 months and up
Pyjamas: Newborn and 3 Month sizes
Warranty: 1 year
Nanit Pro systems include newborn Breathing Wear to start with. Larger sizes are sold separately as your baby grows.
Getting the fit right
Dress your baby in their usual sleepwear.
Put the Band on over the sleepwear, not against the skin.
Check it sits snugly, but not tightly, around the chest.
Make sure the printed pattern faces up towards the camera, with nothing blocking the camera's view of it.
Open the Nanit app and check that breathing motion is showing.
The pyjamas are 100% cotton with a two-way zipper for nappy changes. They should also sit snugly against the chest so the camera has a clear, unobstructed view of the pattern.
Washing and care
Bands and pyjamas are machine washable.
The pyjamas are also dryer safe.
Always follow the care instructions on the garment label.
Check the Band still fits snugly after washing and as your baby grows.
Safe sleep comes first
Nanit Breathing Wear and breathing motion monitoring are not medical devices and are not intended to diagnose, treat or prevent any medical condition, including SIDS. Always follow safe sleep practices, such as placing your baby on their back to sleep and keeping the sleep space clear.

articles.title: Nanit Pro camera: night vision, temperature, humidity and alerts
articles.text:
Your Nanit Pro camera does more than stream video. It also measures the nursery temperature and humidity and sends smart alerts, all through the Nanit app.
Video and night vision
Video: 1080p HD
View: Overhead, bird's-eye view of the cot
Night vision: Automatic infrared night vision
Field of view on the Flex Stand: Wide 130 degree angle
Audio: Two-way audio
Streaming security: 256-bit AES encryption
App: iOS and Android
Night vision switches on automatically, so you can see your baby clearly in a dark room without turning on a light. Two-way audio lets you talk to your baby from the app without going into the room.
Temperature and humidity
The camera continuously measures the nursery temperature and humidity and shows real-time readings on the live view in the app.
Open the Nanit app and go to the live view to see the current readings.
Set your preferred temperature and humidity range in the app.
Turn on notifications so you are told if the room moves outside that range.
With an eligible Nanit Insights membership, review historical trends to see how the room changes overnight.
Trends can show patterns such as a room that warms up after the heating comes on or dries out in winter, which can help you adjust heating, ventilation or sleep clothing.
Smart alerts
You choose which alerts you want and how sensitive they are. The camera can send separate alerts for:
Crying and sound.
Motion.
Standing, when your little one stands up in the cot.
Breathing motion not being detected, when your baby is wearing Breathing Wear and the camera is on a Wall Mount or Floor Stand.
Temperature or humidity moving outside your chosen range.
Live video, two-way audio and alerts work without a Nanit Insights plan.
Watching more than one baby
If you have more than one Nanit camera, the app lets you switch between cameras or view them side by side on a split screen.
Good to know
Nanit is not a medical device. Temperature and humidity readings are extra information about the sleep environment and do not replace safe sleep practices or medical advice.

articles.title: Nanit app: sharing with your Parenting Team and using Care Logs
articles.text:
The Nanit app is free to download on iPhone and Android and connects to your Nanit camera over Wi-Fi. You can share it with the people who help care for your baby and keep a shared log of their day.
Sharing with your Parenting Team
Your Parenting Team is the group of people who can see your camera. Invite a partner, grandparent or nanny so everyone can view the live camera, and on higher Nanit Insights plans they can also see sleep and care history.
Only people you invite to your Parenting Team can view your camera.
You can remove anyone's access instantly from the app.
The number of caregiver accounts depends on your Nanit Insights plan, from up to 2 on the included Sleep plan to unlimited on the Milestones plan.
Logging with Care Logs
Care Logs keeps feeds, naps and nappy changes in one place, so whoever is on duty can see what has already happened. Naps in the cot are logged automatically by the camera. Everything else takes a few taps.
Open the Activity tab in the Nanit app.
Tap the + button in the bottom right corner.
Choose the activity, such as a nappy change, bottle feed, breastfeed or a nap outside the cot.
Follow the prompts to save it.
Anyone on your Parenting Team can view and add to the same Care Log. You can also share a summary with your paediatrician or lactation consultant.
Keeping your camera secure
Video is encrypted between the camera and your phone.
Video and account data are stored in the cloud with encryption and strict access controls.
The app and camera firmware are updated as security threats change, so keep the app up to date.
Use a strong, unique password for your Nanit account.
Connect the camera to a secured, password-protected home Wi-Fi network.

articles.title: Nanit Insights: Sleep Score, Sleep Coach and NextNap explained
articles.text:
Nanit Insights is the optional plan that turns your camera's overnight view into sleep information. Every Nanit camera includes it free for the first 3 months, and the camera keeps working with or without a plan.
Sleep Score
Each morning a Sleep Score out of 100 waits in the Insights tab. The camera detects sleep and wake from the overhead view, so the score is measured rather than filled in by you. It is built from four parts, and each one is shown in the app so you can see what moved the number:
Duration: how long your baby actually slept compared with the time spent in the cot.
Timing: how sleep and wake-ups line up with what is typical for their age and stage.
Continuity: how smooth the night was, including awakenings.
Parent visits: how much help your baby needed from you to settle.
Sleep Coach and trends
Sleep Coach gives personalised, age-based guidance built from your own baby's tracked sleep, with practical steps when you want to change something like bedtime, night wakings or naps. It can be used from the newborn stage. Some patterns show within a few days, and more reliable guidance builds over a few weeks of consistent tracking.
Trends chart bedtime, wake time, night wakings and total sleep over weeks and months, so you can tell a bad night from a bad trend.
NextNap
NextNap predicts your baby's next nap window from how long they slept, when they woke and their patterns over time, combined with age-based norms. It updates through the day as new sleep data comes in, and everyone on your Parenting Team sees the same prediction. It improves the more nights it has to learn from, so treat it as a guide for planning rather than an exact alarm.
What you need
A Nanit Pro camera on a Floor Stand or Wall Mount. Sleep analysis, milestone detection and time-lapse videos need the overhead angle, and a Flex Stand alone is not enough.
An active Nanit Insights plan once the free 3 months ends.
Plans are billed by Nanit Inc. through the Nanit app, separately from your camera purchase, and renew automatically.
You can upgrade, downgrade or cancel at any time in the app, where current Australian pricing is shown.
Good to know
Sleep Coach provides general sleep guidance and is not a medical device. Always follow recommended safe sleep practices.

articles.title: Nanit Sound + Light Machine: set-up, sounds, light and battery
articles.text:
The Nanit Sound + Light Machine combines a sound machine, night light and audio monitor in one compact device. It is designed to help your baby settle and sleep more consistently from newborn through the toddler years.
Using it with or without the app
You do not need a Nanit camera or Wi-Fi to use it. Straight out of the box it works as a standalone sound machine and night light using the built-in buttons.
Connect it to your 2.4GHz home Wi-Fi and the Nanit app to add:
Remote control of sound, light and alerts from your phone, without going into the room.
Cry detection and audio monitoring.
Room temperature tracking.
Routines for wind-down and wake-up.
Sounds and light
Eleven soothing sounds, including white noise, lullabies and nature sounds.
Customisable light colours and brightness.
Night light and an OK to Wake colour function, so your toddler can learn when it is time to get up.
Control from the Sound + Light app, the Nanit Baby Monitor app or the buttons on the device.
Google Home integration, which needs a Nanit Insights plan.
White noise is suitable for babies at an appropriate volume.
Power and battery
The machine runs from mains power through the included adapter, and its built-in rechargeable battery gives up to about 8 hours of cordless use, so you can move it between rooms or take it on a trip.
Specifications and what is in the box
Dimensions: 8.5 x 8.5 x 13 cm
Weight: 365 g
Wi-Fi: 2.4GHz required for app features
Battery: Rechargeable, up to 8 hours
Adapter input: 100 to 240 VAC
Adapter output: 5 VDC, 2.1 A
Cable: USB-C to USB-C, 1.8 m
Account security: Two-step verification required for login
Warranty: 1 year
In the box you will find the Sound + Light Machine with its rechargeable battery, a power adapter and a USB-C to USB-C cable.

articles.title: Nanit Floor Stand: set-up, height and safe placement
articles.text:
The Nanit Floor Stand is a freestanding stand that holds your Nanit Pro camera directly above the cot with no drilling. It suits rentals and nurseries that may be rearranged, and is the most chosen Nanit setup in Australia.
What it does
Gives the overhead, bird's-eye view needed for sleep tracking and breathing motion monitoring with Breathing Wear.
Works in free-standing mode or wall-leaning mode.
Has a compact flat base, about 30 cm wide, that fits under many low cots and bassinets.
Adjusts in height to suit a bassinet, cot or toddler bed as your child grows.
Includes integrated cord covers to keep cables tidy and out of reach.
Works with every Nanit Pro camera sold in Australia, so you can add it to a camera you already own.
What is in the box
Floor Stand main assembly (adjustable stand and base).
Integrated cable management with cord cover.
U-clip wall mount kit, a two-part clip that lets you remove the stand without taking it apart.
Assembly hardware and instructions.
Maximum height: About 170 cm
Base: Compact flat base, about 30 cm wide
Modes: Free-standing and wall-leaning
Set-up time: About 10 minutes for a Pro + Floor Stand system
Warranty: 1 year
Setting it up
Assemble the stand and base following the instructions in the box.
Stand it beside the cot. The compact base fits under many cots.
Set the height so the camera sits directly above the cot.
Attach your Nanit Pro camera and run the cable through the cord covers.
Plug in the power adapter and check the view in the Nanit app, so the whole cot is in view.
Because it is freestanding, you can reposition it or move it to another room if your nursery layout changes.
Placement and safety
The Floor Stand takes up a little floor space and can be within reach of curious little hands, so placement matters more once your baby is mobile. Keep all cables inside the cord covers and out of reach of the cot. Damage caused by incorrect installation is not covered by the warranty.

articles.title: Nanit Wall Mount: installing above the cot
articles.text:
The Nanit Wall Mount fixes your Nanit Pro camera to the wall directly above the cot for a clean, permanent overhead view. It suits a long-term nursery where the cot will stay put.
Why choose the Wall Mount
It gives a consistent overhead position for sleep tracking and breathing motion monitoring with Breathing Wear.
It takes up no floor space, which helps in smaller nurseries.
The camera and cables sit out of your baby's reach once installed.
It works with every Nanit Pro camera sold in Australia, so you can add it to a camera you already own.
Because it is fixed, it is not easily moved without uninstalling it. If you rent or expect to move the cot, the Floor Stand may suit you better.
What is in the kit
Wall Mount bracket for fixed installation above a cot or bassinet.
Cord cover to keep cables tidy and out of reach.
Mounting hardware kit with screws, wall anchors and installation tools or templates.
Step-by-step installation instructions.
Fixing: Two wall anchors (screws and anchors included)
Tools: Drill required
Install time: About 15 minutes
Alignment: Built-in level
Warranty: 1 year
Installing it
Read the installation instructions in the box before you start.
Choose the spot on the wall above the cot, using the template and instructions in the kit.
Use the built-in level to line up the mount.
Drill and fix the mount with the two wall anchors and screws supplied.
Attach your Nanit Pro camera and run the cable through the cord cover channel.
Plug in the power adapter and check the view in the Nanit app, so the whole cot is in view.
Install it securely
The Wall Mount is safe when installed correctly, with the cable kept inside the cord cover and out of reach of the cot. Damage caused by incorrect installation or mounting is not covered by the warranty, so follow the instructions carefully and use the anchors supplied.

articles.title: Nanit Flex Stand and Travel Case: travelling with your Nanit
articles.text:
The Nanit Flex Stand is the portable way to use your Nanit Pro camera at grandparents' houses, on holiday or in a second room. The Floor Stand and Wall Mount systems also include a Flex Stand for travel.
Setting up the Flex Stand
Wrap the flexible gooseneck around a bassinet rail, shelf edge or travel cot.
Clip the camera onto the gooseneck. No tools are needed.
Plug in the camera's power adapter.
Open the Nanit app, connect to the local 2.4GHz Wi-Fi and check the view.
Set-up takes about 5 minutes. When you are done, the Flex Stand folds flat into its pouch for packing.
What works on the Flex Stand
Live HD video with a wide 130 degree view, night vision and two-way audio.
Sound, motion and cry alerts, and temperature and humidity readings.
Breathing motion monitoring does not work on the Flex Stand, because it needs the camera directly above the cot on a Wall Mount or Floor Stand.
Sleep analysis, milestone detection and time-lapse videos also need a Floor Stand or Wall Mount.
The Flex Stand works with Nanit Pro and Nanit Plus cameras and uses the camera's own power supply.
Packing with the Travel Case
The Nanit Travel Case comes in green or grey. It has padded compartments to protect your camera in transit, with room for the Breathing Band, cables and power adapter. It is compact enough for carry-on luggage or a nappy bag.
Flex Stand set-up time: About 5 minutes
Tools needed: None
Travel Case colours: Green or grey
Warranty: 1 year on the Flex Stand and Travel Case
Tips for travelling
Check the Wi-Fi where you are staying is 2.4GHz before you rely on the camera overnight.
Keep the cable well out of reach of the cot or bassinet.
Pack the Breathing Wear so it is ready when you are back on your Wall Mount or Floor Stand at home.
Good to know
Breathing motion alerts are not available while the camera is on the Flex Stand. Always follow safe sleep practices wherever your baby sleeps.

articles.title: Changing modes on your smarTrike as your child grows
articles.text:
Your smarTrike stroller trike is built to change with your child. The Wind and Wonder ranges both move through the same four modes, and you do not need tools for any of the changes. Each change can be reversed just as quickly.
The four modes
Stroller mode, from 6 months on the Wonder max and from 10 months on every other model. The harness is on, the canopy is up and the child handlebar is locked. You steer from the parent handle. The Wonder max is the only model suitable under 10 months, because its seat reclines to 140 degrees. The other models sit upright.
Trike mode, from about 10 months. If the seat is reclined, sit it upright, then unlock the child handlebar. Your child holds on while you keep steering.
Training mode, from about 18 months. Clip the pedals on and fold the canopy away or take it off. Leave the parent handle attached so you can guide and take over when little legs get tired.
Free riding, from about 2 years. Release the parent handle, lift it off and stow the harness. The handle clicks back on if your child needs a push home.
Knowing when to move on
The ages are a guide only, and every child gets there at their own pace. Most toddlers start pushing the pedals between 18 months and 2 years, often one foot at a time or backwards at first. Steady pedalling usually comes between 2 and 3 years. Around ten minutes is a good practice session.
If your child gets frustrated or wants to hop off after a minute, they may not be ready for pedals yet. Go back a mode for a few weeks and try again later.
Move to free riding only once your child can pedal and brake on purpose. Until then, keep a hand on the parent handle.
Handy to know
On the Wonder range and the Wind+, the pedals are detachable. Keep them in the seat pocket when they are not in use.
Your smarTrike folds in every mode, including with the pedals on.

articles.title: Folding and everyday safety checks for your smarTrike
articles.text:
A few quick habits keep every outing on your smarTrike safe and simple. All five smarTrike stroller trikes, in the Wind and Wonder ranges, are tested to stroller safety standards rather than toy standards.
Six habits for every ride
Harness on, every time. Do up the five-point harness in stroller and trike modes, even for a very short walk. It is only stowed away for free riding.
Brake on whenever you stop. Press the rear brake once with your foot to lock it and once more to release it. Use it on flat ground as well as on slopes.
Recline only on the Wonder max. Always have the harness done up when the seat is reclined.
Keep a hand on the parent handle. Hold on until your child can pedal and brake on purpose, which is usually between 2 and 3 years.
Check the locks after every fold. Listen for both clicks when you open the trike, then push.
Register your product. This lets you be contacted about any safety updates.
The bumper bar
The safety bumper bar closes in front of your child and opens with a press, so there is no need to tug at it. You can remove it once your child is riding on their own.
Folding and unfolding
Folding takes about three seconds and needs no tools. Release the fold lock and fold the trike in one motion. It works in every mode, and you can leave the pedals on.
When you open it again, both locks should click into place. Check them before you put your child in and set off.
Steering with one hand
Patented 360° steering lets you steer from the parent handle with one hand, turn on the spot and even go backwards. The shock-absorbing front wheel helps smooth out footpaths and gravel.

articles.title: smarTrike Wonder max: who it suits, the 140° recline and key specs
articles.text:
The Wonder max is the only smarTrike suitable from 6 months, because it is the only model with a seat that reclines to 140°. Here is who it suits, how to use the recline well and the limits to know.
Who the Wonder max suits
The Wonder max suits children from 6 months to about 3 years. A baby who cannot yet sit unaided is supported by the recline and the 5-point harness, which is why it is the one smarTrike to use under 10 months. It also suits toddlers who nap on the move, because the Wonder and Wonder+ sit upright.
Use stroller mode, with you steering, until your child sits up and reaches for the handlebar, usually around 10 months.
Features and specifications
Suitable for: 6 months to about 3 years
Weight: 6.95 kg
Folded size: 54.5 × 26.5 × 38 cm, one piece
Seat: Extra-large, premium cushioned, reclines to 140°
Harness: 5-point with padded straps, plus a safety bumper bar
Canopy: 3-stage, removable for trike mode
Steering: Patented 360° one-handed steering that turns on the spot and reverses
Front wheel: Shock-absorbing
Brake: One-foot rear brake
Frame: Lightweight aluminium, black
Colour: Stone Beige
Certification: Stroller safety standards, not toy standards
Using the recline for naps
At 140° the seat is not flat. It is about the angle of an airline seat fully reclined, so your child's head rests back and the harness holds them, instead of them slumping forward and waking.
When the yawning starts, make sure the parent handle is on so you are steering.
Tip the seat back and pull the canopy forward.
Check the 5-point harness is done up.
Keep walking at the same pace. The motion is what keeps them asleep.
The seat reclines with one hand while you walk, and comes upright again the moment they want to play.
Good to know
The recline is for stroller mode only, with you steering from the parent handle.
The cushioned seat is warmer than mesh. On hot days, recline less and keep the canopy forward.
At 6.95 kg it is the heaviest of the three Wonder models, while still under 7 kg.
Seat fabrics wipe clean with a damp cloth. Store the trike indoors, out of direct sun and damp.
Recline safely
Only recline the seat with the 5-point harness done up, and only in stroller mode with you steering. The Wonder max is the only smarTrike suitable from 6 months.

articles.title: smarTrike Wonder+: who it suits, sun protection and limits
articles.text:
The Wonder+ is the Wonder range model built for long days out and strong Australian sun. It pairs a 3-stage canopy with an extra-large breathable mesh seat.
Who the Wonder+ suits
The Wonder+ suits children from 10 months, once they can sit unaided, to about 3 years. It is the one to choose if your outings are long and sunny. Its seat does not recline, so a baby under 10 months needs the Wonder max instead.
Features and specifications
Suitable for: 10 months to about 3 years
Weight: 6.42 kg
Folded size: 52 × 25.5 × 41 cm, one piece
Seat: Extra-large breathable mesh, the same size as the Wonder max seat
Harness: 5-point with padded shoulder straps, plus a safety bumper bar
Canopy: 3-stage, removable for trike mode
Steering: Patented 360° one-handed steering that turns on the spot and reverses
Front wheel: Shock-absorbing
Brake: One-foot rear brake
Frame: Lightweight aluminium, black
Colour: Sand
Getting the most from the canopy and seat
The canopy extends in three stages and adjusts with one hand.
Pulled fully forward, it shades your child's face and shoulders, even when the sun is low and in their eyes.
It folds flat against the seat when you do not need it, and comes off for trike mode.
The mesh back panel lets warm air move through instead of building up behind your child.
Tips for hot days
Walk before 10am and after 4pm when you can. The footpath in the afternoon is hotter than the air.
Keep the canopy pulled forward.
Never drape a muslin or blanket over the canopy, because it traps heat inside the seat.
Face your child away from the sun when you stop.
On very hot days, trike mode with the canopy off is cooler than stroller mode with the canopy on, as long as you are in the shade.
Flushed cheeks, a hot neck, unusual quiet or fussing and fewer wet nappies are signs to stop. Find shade, offer water and head home. If you are worried, speak with your GP or maternal and child health nurse.
Age limit
The Wonder+ is suitable from 10 months, once your child can sit unaided. Its seat does not recline, so it is not suitable for younger babies.

articles.title: smarTrike Wonder: who it suits, features and limits
articles.text:
The Wonder is the lightest model in the Wonder range at 5.9 kg, made for short walks, school runs and flights. Here is who it suits, what it includes and where its limits are.
Who the Wonder suits
The Wonder suits children from 10 months, once they can sit unaided, to about 3 years. It is the model families fly with most, and the easiest Wonder to carry up stairs, lift into a boot or take onto a tram.
Features and specifications
Suitable for: 10 months to about 3 years
Weight: 5.9 kg
Folded size: 54 × 25 × 34 cm, one piece
Seat: Breathable mesh
Harness: 5-point, plus a safety bumper bar
Canopy: 2-stage, removable for trike mode
Steering: Patented 360° one-handed steering that turns on the spot and reverses
Front wheel: Shock-absorbing
Brake: One-foot rear brake
Frame: Lightweight aluminium, white
Colour: Moonlight, a white frame with a black canopy
Limits to know
The seat does not recline, so the Wonder is not suitable for babies under 10 months. The Wonder max is the model for younger babies.
Because it sits upright, naps in the Wonder tend to be short and slumped.
The 2-stage canopy gives less shade than the 3-stage canopy on the Wonder+ and Wonder max. On long sunny outings, walk in the cooler parts of the day.
Teaching your child to steer
From about 10 months, unlock the child handlebar. Your child holds it while you steer from the parent handle.
From about 18 months, let them turn the handlebar towards things they want. Your hand on the parent handle gently overrides them when needed.
When they pedal continuously and can stop on purpose, usually between 2 and 3, take the parent handle off for the ride out. Put it back on for the tired ride home.
Start on wide, flat paths and leave kerbs and gravel for later.
Harness and brake
Use the 5-point harness every time in stroller and trike modes, and put the rear brake on whenever you stop, even on flat ground.

articles.title: smarTrike Wind and Wind+: features, differences and limits
articles.text:
The Wind and Wind+ are smarTrike's entry range, made for holidays, visits to grandparents and the occasional big day out. They share the patented steering and stroller-standard safety of the Wonder range.
Who they suit
Both suit children from 10 months, once they can sit unaided, to about 3 years. They convert through the same four modes as the Wonder range: stroller, trike, training and free riding.
If you use your trike most days, the Wonder range is built for daily use, with better seat fabrics, upgraded wheels and a sturdier frame.
Wind and Wind+ side by side
Suitable for: 10 months to about 3 years (both)
Weight: Wind 5.6 kg, Wind+ 5.9 kg
Canopy: 2-stage (both)
Harness: 5-point with a safety bumper bar (both)
Steering: Patented 360° one-handed steering with reverse (both)
Frame: Low step-in frame on the Wind+
Child handlebar: Adjustable on the Wind+
Pedals and footrest: Included with both, detachable on the Wind+
Colours: Wind: Aqua, Blush or Black. Wind+: Black
Certification: Stroller safety standards, not toy standards (both)
What the Wind+ adds
A low step-in frame, so your child can climb in by themselves.
An adjustable child handlebar that rises as they grow, keeping the reach right from 10 months to 3 years.
Detachable pedals and footrest: off for scooting, on for pedalling, and off again for the car boot.
The Wind+ is a Baby Bunting exclusive and is not sold on the smarTrike website. It carries the same 2-year Australian warranty as every smarTrike, handled by our team in Braeside.
In the box
Both come with the trike with the seat and harness fitted, the detachable parent handle, the 2-stage canopy, the pedals, the footrest and a quick-start guide. Assembly needs no tools: the wheels click on, and the parent handle slides in and locks. The Wind is the lightest trike smarTrike sells, and it folds in one motion and stands on its own.
Ages and safety
The Wind and Wind+ are suitable from 10 months to about 3 years. Their seats do not recline, so they are not for babies who cannot yet sit unaided. Use the 5-point harness every time in stroller and trike modes.

articles.title: smarTrike Xtend Ride-on and Xtend Mini+ scooter: stages and ages
articles.text:
The Xtend range picks up where the stroller trike leaves off. The Xtend Ride-on starts as a parent-controlled ride-on at 12 months, and the Xtend Mini+ is an extendable scooter from 2 years.
Xtend Ride-on: four stages
Parent-controlled ride-on, from 12 months. Your child sits on the seat while you guide with the parent handle.
Ride-on. Take the parent handle off when they are ready, and they push along with their feet.
Three-wheel scooter. Remove the seat and extend the handlebar.
Two-wheel scooter, for big kids up to about 12 years.
Every change is a click or a lock, so no tools are needed. The handlebars adjust and extend as your child grows, the wheels are no-puncture, and there is storage under the seat.
Xtend Mini+ scooter
The Xtend Mini+ is an extendable scooter that grows with your child from 2 to 9 years. It starts as a three-wheel scooter and converts to two wheels when they are ready.
The stem height adjusts as they grow.
The handlebar and deck both extend.
No-puncture wheels are smooth on footpaths and quiet indoors.
It folds flat for the car boot, under the bed or onto the bus.
Ages and colours
Xtend Ride-on ages: 12 months to about 12 years
Xtend Ride-on colours: Blue, Pink, Teal, Cool Grey, Soft green
Xtend Mini+ ages: 2 to 9 years
Xtend Mini+ colours: Green, Pink, Blue, Grey
Warranty in Australia: 2 years
What is in the box
The Xtend Ride-on comes with the ride-on with its seat, the parent handle, the scooter deck and stem, and a quick-start guide. The Xtend Mini+ comes with the scooter, its adjustable stem and a quick-start guide.
Ages
The Xtend Ride-on is suitable from 12 months as a parent-controlled ride-on, and the Xtend Mini+ from 2 years as a three-wheel scooter. Keep the parent handle on the Ride-on until your child is ready to ride on their own.

articles.title: Assembling your smarTrike: what is in the box, manuals and spare parts
articles.text:
Most parents put their smarTrike together in under ten minutes, with no tools. Here is what to expect, where to find the manual and what to do if a part is missing.
What is in the box
The Wonder, Wonder+, Wonder max, Wind and Wind+ cartons contain:
The trike frame, with the seat, harness and bumper bar already fitted.
The detachable parent handle.
The canopy: 2-stage on the Wonder, Wind and Wind+, and 3-stage on the Wonder+ and Wonder max.
The pedals and footrest.
The quick-start guide.
Putting it together
Unpack everything and check it against the list above before you start.
Click the wheels on.
Slide the parent handle in until it locks.
Before the first ride, do up the 5-point harness and try the rear brake: press once to lock and once to release.
The smarTrike manuals page lists a manual for each model sold in Australia, covering assembly, the four modes, folding and care. If you cannot download the one you need, send us a request with your model name.
Which model do I have?
The model name is printed on the frame near the parent handle, and on the box. If you are still unsure, include a photo of your trike when you send us a request.
Spare parts
Spare parts are available for the models sold in Australia, and most are in stock in Braeside:
Wheels: the shock-absorbing front wheel and the rear wheels for the Wonder, Wonder+ and Wonder max.
Canopies: 2-stage for the Wonder and 3-stage for the Wonder+ and Wonder max, in the matching colour.
Harness parts: the 5-point harness, buckles and the bumper bar release.
Pedals and the folding footrest.
The complete parent handle, with the 360° steering coupling.
For anything not listed, send a photo and your model name and we will source it.
Damaged on arrival
If a part is missing or damaged when your trike arrives, report it within 48 hours of delivery with photos. A faulty product is a warranty matter, not a change of mind return, and it is quicker to sort.

articles.title: Flying with your smarTrike Wonder: carry-on, folded sizes and airport tips
articles.text:
Every Wonder model folds in about three seconds to a single piece designed for the aircraft overhead locker. Here is what to check before you fly and how to make the airport easier.
Folded sizes and weights
Wonder: 54 × 25 × 34 cm, 5.9 kg
Wonder+: 52 × 25.5 × 41 cm, 6.42 kg
Wonder max: 54.5 × 26.5 × 38 cm, 6.95 kg
Each one folds to a single piece with nothing to detach. These sizes are for the Wonder range only.
Before you book
The Wonder range is carry-on approved and designed for the overhead locker, but cabin allowances vary by airline and fare. Compare your fare's cabin allowance with the folded size of your model before you fly. We do not list airline allowances because they change, so your airline's own website is the one to trust.
Keep your model's folded size handy, as gate staff may ask for it.
At the airport
Ride it to the gate. Security will X-ray it folded.
Fold it at the aircraft door. It takes about three seconds and there is nothing to reassemble.
Lift it into the overhead locker, wheels in first.
Unfold it at the arrival gate, and your child rides on from there.
If it goes in the hold
If the trike cannot travel in the cabin, it goes in the hold as a stroller. Ask for a gate check so you can use it right to the aircraft door and get it back at the aircraft when you land.
The same fold works on trains, trams and stairs: fold, carry and unfold.
Which model to take
The Wonder, at 5.9 kg, is the model families fly with most. Choose the Wonder max if your child is under 10 months or sleeps on the move, because it is the only one that reclines.
Travel damage
If your trike is damaged in transit, report it within 48 hours with photos. Transit damage is a carrier matter, but we will help with parts.

articles.title: smarTrike warranty in Australia and registering your product
articles.text:
Every smarTrike bought in Australia is covered for two years, on top of your rights under Australian Consumer Law. Claims are handled by our team in Braeside, Victoria.
What is covered
The warranty covers manufacturing faults under normal domestic use, including:
Frame defects and structural faults.
Faults in the steering, brake or folding mechanism.
Faulty wheels, bearings or shock absorber.
A defective harness, buckles or bumper bar release.
Seat fabric or a canopy that fails through a manufacturing fault.
Cover applies to every smarTrike sold in Australia, including the Wind+ bought at Baby Bunting.
What is not covered
Normal wear and tear, including tyre and fabric wear.
Damage from misuse, neglect, accident or impact.
Use beyond the stated age or weight limits.
Modification or unauthorised repairs.
Fading or corrosion from outdoor or damp storage.
Second-hand purchases.
Commercial or hire use.
How to make a claim
Gather your proof of purchase, the model name and a few photos or a short video of the fault.
Send us a request with those details attached.
We will repair it, send a replacement part or replace the product. Most claims are sorted without the product going anywhere, usually with a part in the post.
Registering your smarTrike
You do not need to register to be covered, because the warranty applies from the date of purchase. Registering takes about a minute and gives you:
Your receipt on file, so you will not need to find it if you ever claim.
Safety updates sent to you directly, not through a retailer.
Faster claims, because we already have your model and purchase date.
Optional monthly guides from the Learn hub, matched to your child's age.
The form asks for your name, email, model, purchase date, where you bought it, and a photo or PDF of your receipt (PDFs up to 4 MB). A mobile number and your child's date of birth are optional.
Faulty on arrival
If your smarTrike arrives faulty or damaged, report it within 48 hours of delivery with photos. That is a warranty matter rather than a change of mind return, and it is quicker to sort.
